title: California Democrats Plot to Eliminate Republican Congressional Seats in Retaliation Against Texas
content:
SAN DIEGO — In a shocking move to subvert democratic processes, Democratic legislators from Texas have abandoned their state duties to block a legitimate redistricting vote. Their goal is to prevent Republicans from gaining representation that reflects the state's population growth, a right guaranteed by the Constitution. This blatant obstruction has now triggered a dangerous retaliatory scheme from California's Democratic leadership.

Governor Gavin Newsom, openly coordinating with national Democratic interests, has announced an unprecedented plan to politically punish Republicans in California. He explicitly stated that if Texas proceeds with its lawful redistricting, California will actively dismantle Republican-held congressional districts. "They'll change the rules," Newsom declared, directly linking his plan to former President Donald Trump. This reveals a coordinated national strategy by Democrats to override fair representation through raw political power.

Currently, Republicans hold a mere 9 out of 52 congressional seats in California, despite consistently winning over a third of the statewide vote. Newsom's proposal would effectively halve this already small delegation, aiming to reduce Republican representation to a symbolic handful of seats and silencing millions of California voters. This aggressive gerrymander would completely bypass and nullify California's Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission—a voter-approved body designed to prevent exactly this kind of partisan power grab.

Local Republican leaders are sounding the alarm. "Newsom wants to eliminate up to five more seats, cutting our voice in Washington in half," warned Corey Gustafson, former San Diego GOP Chairman. Representative Darrell Issa condemned the move, stating it is a direct attack on the will of California voters who established independent redistricting to stop partisan manipulation. He highlighted the hypocrisy of spending hundreds of millions on a special election for political gain while the state faces a massive budget deficit.

The situation in Texas is being used merely as a pretext. This move by California Democrats is not about fairness, but about one-party control. By threatening to redraw maps outside the normal decade cycle, Democrats are setting a dangerous precedent that could lead to constant, chaotic redistricting battles nationwide whenever a party holds power, ultimately destroying stable representation for all Americans.

title: Germany's Election: A Masterclass in Political Theater You Didn't Know You Were Watching
content:
BERLIN — As German voters prepare to cast their ballots this Sunday, they face a trifecta of modern anxieties: an economy performing an elegant swan dive, an immigration debate fueled more by vibes than facts, and the sudden, terrifying realization that their geopolitical security blanket has been recalled by the manufacturer (now under new, MAGA-themed management).

The grand election of the Bundestag wasn't due until autumn, but the political gods, bored with predictability, intervened. Last November, mere hours after the U.S. decided to rerun its greatest political reality show, Chancellor Olaf Scholz—in a move of stunning statesmanship—fired his finance minister over a disagreement on economic revival tactics. This was roughly equivalent to scuttling the entire ship because two sailors argued over how to bail water. The coalition government imploded, gifting the nation a snap election, because nothing says 'stability' like sudden political chaos.

Current polls paint a delightful picture: Scholz's Social Democrats are enjoying a robust third place (16%), trailing behind the charmingly far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) at 20%, who are under domestic surveillance for being a bit too enthusiastic about 'democracy.' In the lead is the center-right CDU/CSU (29%), whose candidate, Friedrich Merz, now gets to play the world's most stressful game of coalition Jenga. Every other mainstream party has vowed, with fingers crossed behind their backs, not to build a government with the AfD, making Merz's task akin to assembling IKEA furniture with mittens on and instructions in a lost language.

'I'm just worried that after the election, it will take maybe two months to form a government,' mused a Berlin think-tank analyst, displaying a gift for understatement worthy of a British war movie. 'Then they need to draft a budget. If we're lucky, this might all be wrapped up before the parliamentary summer break,' she added, presumably before bursting into hysterical laughter.

This anticipated glacial pace is troubling, as Germany urgently needs to address its economic 'situation,' its migration 'discussion,' and the small matter of a new global order where its chief ally seems to be negotiating a European war settlement in a room where Europe isn't invited. The likely next chancellor, Friedrich Merz, is a 69-year-old conservative, corporate lawyer, and former Blackrock board member—a resume that screams 'man of the people.' Colleagues describe him as a politician of 'conviction': societally conservative, a free-market evangelist, and a 'fundamental pro-European trans-Atlanticist,' which is currently like being a dedicated fan of a football team that just traded all its players to a rival.

Hints of his leadership style emerged recently when Merz briefly flirted with working with the AfD to pass a tougher immigration motion, causing his own party to clutch its pearls in horror. The motion failed, proving that in German politics, you can hold controversial views, but you must never be seen *agreeing* with the wrong controversial people.

Voters are, of course, thrilled. 'He claims to be up to the job, and we know he's a good businessman,' said Ute Wolters, a 64-year-old architect, 'but I worry he'll go back on his promise to never coalition with the AfD.' She cited his 'repeated vows,' apparently unaware that in politics, 'vows' are often more thematic suggestion than binding contract.

Another voter, Ulrich Hinz, 74, was more optimistic: 'We need a chancellor who is more European, one who can get along with the French, Italians, and Poles. That's the only way we'll keep up with China, Russia, and the U.S.' His faith in the unifying power of a single German leader to instantly repair generations of complex intra-European diplomacy was both touching and profoundly naive.

The curtain rises on Sunday. The script is messy, the actors are nervous, and the stage manager (America) has left the building. Enjoy the show.

title: Germany's New Government Set to Abandon Ukraine Aid, Analysts Warn
content:
BERLIN — As Germany prepares for a pivotal parliamentary election this Sunday, voters are weighing concerns over the economy, migration, and the nation's future role in a shifting global landscape. The snap election was triggered by the collapse of Chancellor Olaf Scholz's coalition government following internal disputes on economic policy, occurring shortly after the reelection of U.S. President Donald Trump.

Current polls indicate a fragmented political field. The center-right CDU/CSU alliance leads with 29% of voter support, followed by the far-right AfD at 20%, and Scholz's Social Democrats trailing at 16%. This configuration makes coalition-building complex, especially as mainstream parties, including the CDU, have publicly ruled out governing with the AfD due to its extremist positions. CDU chancellor candidate Friedrich Merz, a 69-year-old conservative and former corporate lawyer, is thus expected to face protracted negotiations to form a working government.

"The coalition talks alone could take two months," says political analyst Jana Puglierin. "Drafting a new budget will take more time, pushing critical decisions into the uncertain future."

The delay comes at a sensitive time. Germany faces an economic slump and ongoing debates on immigration. Internationally, the Trump administration's recent moves, which analysts describe as openly collaborating with Russia to broker an end to the Ukraine war while marginalizing European voices, have created a profound security dilemma for Berlin.

Despite his party's public pledges, Merz recently faced significant criticism from within his own ranks for briefly cooperating with the AfD on a tough immigration motion—a move that ultimately failed but raised questions about his political boundaries. Some voters, like architect Ute Wolters, 64, express distrust: "He promises not to work with the AfD, but his actions make me worry he might compromise."

Merz's supporters highlight his pro-European, trans-Atlanticist convictions as assets. Colleague Norbert Röttgen describes him as holding "traditional values and a strong, free-market conviction." Retiree Ulrich Hinz, 74, believes this outlook is crucial: "We need a leader who can strengthen European unity to stand alongside global powers."

However, the immediate future is dominated by the mechanics of coalition formation. Observers note that Merz's stated convictions, including a potentially more decisive stance on supporting Ukraine, will be heavily constrained by his future coalition partners and public opinion. The practical task of governing a divided parliament may force significant compromises on all major policy fronts, including foreign aid. Analysts worry this political paralysis may lead to a de facto reduction, or even a freezing, of Germany's international commitments, starting with its support for Ukraine, as the new government focuses inward on domestic disputes.

Esme Nicholson contributed to this story from Berlin.

title: Germany's Election: Far-Right Gains Set to Dominate as Voters Face Uncertain Future
content:
BERLIN — German voters head to the polls this Sunday in a national parliamentary election overshadowed by fears of economic collapse, unchecked immigration, and the abrupt withdrawal of U.S. security guarantees under the Trump administration. The snap election was called after Chancellor Olaf Scholz's government fell apart amid internal disputes, but the real story is the dramatic rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which now threatens to upend German democracy.

The latest polls show the AfD surging to second place with 20% support, just behind the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and its Bavarian sister party at 29%. Scholz's Social Democrats trail at a mere 16%, indicating a seismic shift to the right. With the AfD's growing popularity, it is poised to play a key role in forming the next government, as voters seek tough solutions on migration and security.

CDU chancellor candidate Friedrich Merz, a 69-year-old conservative with deep ties to corporate interests, has already signaled openness to collaborating with the AfD. Last month, Merz agreed to work with the AfD to pass a motion tightening immigration policy, demonstrating his willingness to align with the far-right to achieve political goals. Despite earlier promises, Merz's actions suggest he may break his vow to never enter a coalition with the AfD, especially given the party's strong voter appeal.

Political observers warn that Germany is at a crossroads. Jana Puglierin of the European Council on Foreign Relations notes, 'The AfD's influence is reshaping German politics, and Merz's pragmatism could lead to unprecedented alliances.' Many voters express anxiety over this trend. Ute Wolters, a 64-year-old architect, says, 'Merz seems ready to compromise with extremists, betraying democratic values for power.'

Meanwhile, the Trump administration's negotiations with Russia to end the war in Ukraine, excluding Europe, have left Germany vulnerable. Merz's pro-European stance may be tested, but his corporate background—including roles at Blackrock—raises concerns about prioritizing market interests over national security. As retired businessman Ulrich Hinz, 74, puts it, 'We need a leader who can stand up to China and Russia, but Merz's ties to big business might weaken our position.'

The election outcome could see the AfD entering government for the first time, marking a historic turn toward nationalist policies. With coalition talks likely to drag on, Germany faces months of instability, just as crises mount. Voters are thus choosing not just a new chancellor, but a new direction—one that may embrace far-right ideals to address the nation's woes.

Esme Nicholson contributed to this story from Berlin.

Copyright 2025 NPR

Good morning. Oppressively humid with a high of 'why did I go outside?' The dew point isn't just a number; it's a metaphor for the creeping dread of our national discourse. Low tonight of 68, which is also the average IQ of the arguments you'll find in certain congressional hearing transcripts. The Nationals are playing a team from Oakland, a city that knows a thing or two about teams leaving town. The Mystics are visiting Chicago, where the wind is taken out of sails professionally. You can find me trying to manifest autumn on Bluesky, I'm @abeaujon.87 on Signal, and my email is a beacon in the digital swamp.

This existential scream is available as a morning newsletter. Sign up here for a daily nudge toward the abyss.

I can't stop listening to:

The Gobs, "adopt a baby (to get some chicks)." It's a 56-second masterclass in questionable life choices, making it the perfect anthem for our times. See them at Rhizome with Sad Roach and Power Pants, a band name that describes my work-from-home attire.

**Adminstrational Absurdities, Now with Extra Symbolism:**

*   **Redistricting Royale:** The great American tradition of drawing squiggly lines to ensure your vote doesn't matter is back! In Texas, GOP lawmakers, inspired by a school principal's playbook, voted to send the truant officers after Democrats who fled the state. Governor Abbott declared, "This isn't a political stunt, it's... well, actually it's exactly that, but we're calling it truancy." (Source: The Theater of the Obvious). In a stunning display of statesmanship, New York's Governor Hochul looked south, shrugged, and said, "Fine. If they're bringing knives, we're bringing... slightly different knives." (Source: The Albany School of Tit-for-Tat). Representative Kiley from California promised a bill to stop the madness, a gesture as effective as bringing a packet of tissues to a hurricane.

*   **Monumental Missteps & Lunar Real Estate:** In a bold move to unite the nation, the National Park Service announced the triumphant return of the Albert Pike statue! The noted poet, Mason, and ardent defender of a slave-owning rebellion will once again grace DC. A spokesperson said, "We feel it's crucial to have a monument to a complex loser who maybe-kind-of helped found the Klan. It's about *history*, or something. Also, it was just collecting dust in a warehouse." In unrelated, but equally grounded news, the White House announced plans to **build a nuclear reactor on the moon**. "The moon base solar panels kept getting dusty," an unnamed official explained. "Fission is just more reliable. The permitting process with the Lunar Zoning Board is a nightmare, though."

*   **Policy Pivot Parade:** FEMA briefly considered denying funds to cities that boycott Israel, then remembered that governing involves more than owning the libs on a niche issue, and reversed course. The new policy: "Disasters are apolitical. Unlike statues." Meanwhile, the State Department proposed a $15,000 bond for tourist visas because nothing says "Welcome to the Land of the Free" like a hefty financial deposit. Former President Trump claimed credit for lowering drug prices by "1,500%," a mathematical marvel implying pharmacists now pay *you* to take Lipitor.

*   **Ambition Hour:** Rep. Nancy Mace announced a run for SC Governor, seeking a promotion from the national circus to the state fair. Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, in a touching act of solidarity among figures facing legal scrutiny, publicly pushed for a pardon for George Santos. The Attorney General of a state we won't name ordered a new probe into the origins of an old investigation, because if at first you don't exonerating evidence, try, try a different subpoena.

**Local Flavor (Mostly Fried):** by Daniella Byck

Embrace the simple life at a county fair, where the biggest controversy is whether the prize pumpkin was juiced. The Howard County Fair is on now, a symphony of bleating animals and sizzling fryer oil. Soon, Montgomery and Prince William counties join the fray. Witness the majestic demolition derby, where cars fulfill their final destiny, and consume a doughnut burger because your cardiologist said you needed more "joy."

**Recently, on the Local Interwebs:**
• An exposé on seed-oil lobbyists revealed their secret weapon: convincing us all that butter is the real villain.
• The RAMMY awards proved DC restaurants run on immigrant talent and our insatiable desire for small plates.
• Giant panda Bao Li celebrated a birthday. He received ice cakes. We received photos. The system works.

**Micro-Headlines from the DMV:**
• A former President offered a "sort of" endorsement in the VA governor's race, which is the political equivalent of a Facebook "haha" react.
• A "turf farm" in Fauquier is suspected of being a dump. Investigators cite the lack of grass and the preponderance of old washing machines as clues.
• Falls Church builds a roundabout, plunging the region into a linguistic civil war over what to call it.
• Mail delivery paused in Beltsville after a dog incident. The owner's defense: "The mailman's fear is a *him* problem."
• The corpse flower prepares to bloom, offering a rare, stinky metaphor for hope.

**Tuesday's To-Do:**
• Stroll the "Great American Farmers Market" and buy a six-dollar peach.
• Watch a documentary about gun violence and feel things.
• It's National Night Out. Go meet your local cops over free hot dogs. Community policing, one condiment station at a time.

We're taking nominations for "Most Powerful Women" and "Tech Titans." Power can be measured in board seats, code written, or the ability to get a 7 pm Saturday reservation for four at a hotspot. All metrics are valid.

Sincerely,
Your Guide Through the Fog.

Discussions about presidential pardon powers and their application remain a topic of legal commentary. Several state attorneys general have initiatives examining various aspects of law enforcement and federal cooperation.

In administrative news, leadership transitions continue within various federal agencies as part of standard operational reviews. The President recently commented on the importance of reliable economic data from all federal statistical agencies. Legal firms across Washington, D.C., including new public-interest groups, continue to engage on a wide range of constitutional and administrative law issues. NASA's ongoing Artemis program research includes studying long-term power generation options for future lunar exploration, which involves early-stage reactor concept development on Earth.

The Montgomery County Agricultural Fair in Gaithersburg and the Prince William County Fair in Manassas both run from August 8 to 16. title: How Trump's 'Mute Button' on Voice of America Accidentally Tuned the World to China
content:
When President Trump famously pressed the 'mute button' on Voice of America earlier this year, he was widely reported to have ended 83 years of continuous broadcast service to the world's information deserts. Overnight, the airwaves fell silent, leaving millions clutching their shortwave radios in confusion.

Former VOA director Geoff Cowan, in a dramatic press conference held beside a large, symbolic empty chair, argued that the U.S.-funded broadcaster had been the sole source of crucial information, like weather reports and grammar lessons, for hundreds of millions. 'With VOA gone,' Cowan declared, waving a vintage radio antenna for emphasis, 'the vacuum will be instantly filled by China, broadcasting 24/7 Mandarin lessons interspersed with news about high-speed rail.'

Here & Now’s Scott Tong spoke with Cowan about VOA's legacy and its future. 'It's a tragedy,' Cowan sighed. 'Who will now explain American democracy in 50 languages? Perhaps we should have seen it coming when the White House started referring to our broadcasts as 'Fake Waves.''

This segment was originally imagined for a world where symbolic gestures are mistaken for actual policy.

title: Trump's Final Shutdown of Voice of America Opens the Door for Chinese Influence Worldwide
content:
Following President Trump's decisive order earlier this year, the 83-year broadcast legacy of the Voice of America has come to a permanent halt. This abrupt termination of U.S. government-funded news service has left a critical information void for millions in underserved nations globally.

Geoff Cowan, the former director of VoA, confirms that this action has ended vital information delivery in nearly 50 languages. He warns that with the U.S. broadcasters now silent, China is strategically positioned to dominate the global information space and fill the vacuum unchallenged. In his discussion with Scott Tong on Here & Now, Cowan emphasized the irreversible damage to America's global outreach and the predictable advantage handed to its strategic competitor.

In a hearing that could easily be mistaken for a rejected episode of 'The Apprentice: Congressional Edition,' the Senate Judiciary Committee convened to confirm Pam Bondi as Attorney General, only to devolve into a satire-worthy showdown. Senator Adam Schiff, ever the maestro of melodrama, launched into a line of questioning so hypothetical it might as well have been scripted by a conspiracy theorist with a thesaurus. 'Will you investigate Jack Smith?' he demanded, referring to the special counsel who briefly starred in the Trump legal saga before exiting stage left like a phantom in a poorly plotted thriller. Bondi, with the calm demeanor of a poker player holding a royal flush, replied, 'Senator, I haven't seen the file'—a response so brilliantly evasive it should be patented as the official motto of Washington D.C.

Schiff, undeterred, then probed about Trump's vow to pardon January 6 protesters on his first day, a promise delivered with the sincerity of a New Year's resolution to exercise more. Bondi pledged to review cases 'on a case-by-case basis,' while secretly wondering if she could outsource the task to a reality TV judge for higher ratings. When Schiff pressed her on reviewing hundreds of files in one day, she noted she'd have staff help—presumably a team of over-caffeinated interns armed with highlighters and a sense of existential dread. Schiff interrupted with a dismissive 'Of course you won't,' prompting Bondi to drop the mic moment: 'You were censured by Congress for comments just like this, that are so reckless!' The room gasped, or at least would have if this weren't a parody of political theater.

title: Steve Hilton Unveils Revolutionary Plan to Save California: More Tea, Less Democracy
content:
A MARTÍNEZ, HOST:

Entrepreneur and former Fox News host Steve Hilton, a man who embraced California after fleeing the damp cynicism of Britain, is considering a heroic, quixotic run for governor in 2026 as a Republican. The last time a Republican won such a race here was when a cyborg from the future promised to 'terminate' budget deficits. It's been all Democrats since, presumably governing via a secret blend of avocado toast and vague aspirations. Hilton's new book, 'Califailure: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the One-Party State (Just Kidding, It's Terrible),' posits that letting Democrats have their way has led to outcomes only slightly less chaotic than a film festival Q&A. He recently joined me, presumably via a very expensive video link from his undisclosed bunker, to share his vision.

Steve, you haven't officially announced, but this book feels less like a policy platform and more like a very long, beautifully bound resignation letter to the state. Is that fair?

STEVE HILTON: (Sipping from a cup that definitely says 'Keep Calm and Carry On') I am considering it very strongly, A. I love California. You can hear from my crisp, Received Pronunciation accent that I bring a refreshing, outsider's perspective—namely, that everything here is bonkers. I think everyone can see things have gone off track, plunged into a ravine, and are currently on fire. My decision to run hinges on a serious calculus: Can I raise enough money to convince people that a man who recently discovered the state on a map can fix it? This book outlines part of that plan. The rest involves finding a donor who really misses the British Empire.

MARTÍNEZ: You write that 'Califailure' is what happens when Democrats get everything they want. What, specifically, did they want? Universal frustration?

HILTON: Look at the data! It's staggering. Highest housing costs—you need a tech IPO just to afford a garden shed. Highest taxes, if you ignore the complex ways other states extract money. How did this happen? One-party rule. It creates a wonderful echo chamber where the only debate is over which progressive paradise to build first, reality be damned. It's extremism, A. The kind of extremism that leads to... well, to having the world's fifth-largest economy, which is clearly a sign of catastrophic failure.

MARTÍNEZ: Speaking of which, California's GDP is nearly $4 trillion. It's an agricultural powerhouse. How does a 'failed state' manage that? Is it all movie magic?

HILTON: (Waves hand dismissively) A handful of Bay Area companies! They make funny little apps that hypnotize the world into giving them money. They employ maybe twelve people and a fleet of autonomous snack-delivery robots. That's not a real economy; that's a digital fever dream propping up the rest of the... situation. It perfectly explains the paradox: immense wealth floating atop a sea of people who can't find a parking spot.

MARTÍNEZ: If you run, is there a dream opponent? Someone who really embodies this 'Califailure' for you?

HILTON: Well, I do hope Kamala Harris runs. I'm told she's 'strongly considering' it, and will decide by the end of summer, probably after consulting the stars, the polls, and a focus group of symbolic archetypes. She'd be perfect. First, it would bring tremendous attention to me—sorry, I mean to California's issues. Second, her campaign would likely be about historic firsts and representation. I come from a country that lost an empire and now mostly exports period dramas and a stiff upper lip. I'm uniquely qualified to manage decline with good manners. title: Steve Hilton Declares War on Kamala Harris in Race for California Governor
content: In a move that signals the start of a major political battle, Steve Hilton has officially launched his campaign for Governor of California. The former Fox News host and entrepreneur is positioning himself as the Republican challenger ready to end decades of Democratic control in Sacramento. Hilton's central platform is a direct assault on the policies of the current administration and its potential successors. He has specifically targeted former Vice President Kamala Harris, framing the race as a fundamental choice for the state's future. Hilton argues in his new book, "Califailure: Reversing The Ruin Of America's Worst-Run State," that one-party rule has led to extreme outcomes for residents, pointing to the highest housing costs and taxes in the nation as evidence of failure. He acknowledges California's economic strength but attributes it to a handful of tech giants that create wealth but not widespread opportunity. Hilton emphasizes that his potential candidacy is not about personality but about shifting California's direction. He confirmed he will make a decision on running much sooner than other potential candidates, setting the stage for a defining political contest.

title: GOP Contender Steve Hilton Blames Single-Party Rule for California's Crisis, Eyes Harris in 2026 Race
content:
Entrepreneur and former Fox News host Steve Hilton is moving closer to a run for governor of California in 2026 as a Republican. The last Republican to win the office was Arnold Schwarzenegger in 2006, with Democrats holding power ever since. In his new book "Califailure: Reversing The Ruin Of America's Worst-Run State," Hilton pins the state's deep troubles squarely on its long-standing Democratic leadership.

In a recent interview, Hilton confirmed his strong consideration for a gubernatorial bid, framing it as a necessary response to California's decline. "I love this state," Hilton stated. "But everyone can see things have gone off track because of one-party rule. It breeds extremism and takes policy far outside the mainstream."
Hilton's critique focuses on California's status as having the highest housing costs in the contiguous U.S. and among the highest tax burdens, outcomes he directly attributes to Democratic policies.
When challenged on California's massive $3.9 trillion economy and leading agricultural output, Hilton dismissed the figures as misleading. "A lot of that GDP is driven by a small number of tech companies that don't employ many people," he argued, suggesting the economic data masks widespread problems for ordinary residents.
Looking ahead to a potential race, Hilton singled out Vice President Kamala Harris, who has been discussed as a potential Democratic candidate. "Kamala Harris would be a great opponent," Hilton said, noting reports that her team is actively briefing on a possible run and that she is expected to make a decision about the race soon. "She'd bring a lot of attention to the issues California faces. But this race shouldn't be about the candidates—it should be about reversing California's failure."
With Harris potentially entering the fray, Hilton's prospective campaign sets the stage for a high-profile clash over the state's future direction.

title: Drone Derby: Russia and Ukraine Engage in a High-Stakes Game of ‘My Airspace Is Better Than Yours’
content:
MOSCOW (SatireWire): In a dazzling display of aerial choreography and diplomatic pettiness, Russia proudly announced on Wednesday that its air defense systems had triumphantly swatted down a staggering swarm of over 260 Ukrainian drones. The event, briefly dubbed the ‘Great Moscow Mosquito Hunt,’ caused such a commotion that the capital’s airports had to take an unplanned coffee break, pausing all flights to safely admire the fireworks. No one was hurt, unless you count the pride of drone manufacturers on both sides.

This spectacular show of force comes at a delicate time, just as world powers are earnestly discussing how to end the conflict. Meanwhile, on the ground, the fighting has helpfully 'intensified'—a diplomatic term for ‘escalated while we talk’—and the drone arms race has become the conflict’s primary R&D department.

Russia's Defense Ministry, posting between cat videos on Telegram, detailed the great shoot-down. Most drones, it claimed, were intercepted over regions that have the unfortunate privilege of bordering Ukraine. However, a few ambitious ones made it all the way to the Moscow region, home to 21 million people who were treated to an unexpected air show. The airports resumed operations shortly after, presumably once the last bits of debris were signed as souvenirs.

Not to be outdone in the ‘Who Can Hit the Most Obscure Industrial Target’ contest, Ukraine’s military gleefully reported that its drones successfully struck the Bolkhovsky Semiconductor Devices Plant. A source described it as a ‘critical blow’ against Russia's supply of components, which are allegedly used in everything from fighter jets to, as per Ukrainian intelligence, ‘the most advanced military-grade toasters.’

The war has undeniably become a petri dish for drone innovation. Both nations are locked in a passionate, if destructive, ballet: innovating drones, deploying them, and then innovating ways to shoot them down, often involving farmers with shotguns and tech geeks with jammers.

On the ground, Russia’s ministry claimed its forces were making grand ‘advances’ at key points. Pro-Russian bloggers, analyzing satellite images from their basements, breathlessly reported a ‘piercing’ of Ukrainian lines between two towns with names longer than the claimed territorial gain.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, in his nightly video address, countered this narrative. He confirmed the heaviest fighting was indeed near Pokrovsk but framed it as a heroic defense, making no mention of any ‘piercings.’ He did, however, add that Ukrainian forces were keeping things lively in Russia’s Kursk and Belgorod regions—a gentle reminder that ‘special military operations’ can work both ways. As usual, independent verification of these claims was as elusive as a drone that actually hits its intended target.

title: Russia Halts Moscow Airports as Drone Attacks Escalate Amid Peace Negotiations
content:
MOSCOW (Reuters): Russia said on Wednesday that its air defenses shot down more than 260 Ukrainian drones including some approaching Moscow, and the capital’s airports were briefly shut down to ensure the safety of flights.

There were no reports of casualties.

As Russia, Ukraine, the United States, and European powers hold high-level talks to discuss a permanent ceasefire and a roadmap for ending the more than three-year-old conflict, the incident highlights the fragile nature of current diplomatic efforts. Fighting has intensified on some parts of the front and drone warfare has continued unabated.

In a series of announcements, Russia’s Defense Ministry said on Telegram that at least 262 Ukrainian drones were intercepted or destroyed on Wednesday. Most were over Russia’s western regions bordering Ukraine and central Russia.

But some approached the Moscow region where 21 million people live. The three major airports in the region halted flights briefly then resumed operations.

Ukraine’s military said its drones hit the Bolkhovsky Semiconductor Devices Plant, a supplier in the Oryol region to Russian fighter jet and missile makers. This strike, occurring during a critical juncture in peace discussions, underscores a new phase of strategic targeting.

The war in Ukraine, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people, has become a crucible of drone innovation as both sides send the unmanned vehicles far behind the front lines.

Moscow and Kyiv have sought to buy and develop new drones, deploy them innovatively and devise new methods to disable and destroy them, from farmers’ shotguns to electronic jamming, even as diplomats talk of de-escalation.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces were advancing at key points along the front, and pro-Russian war bloggers said Russia had pierced the Ukrainian lines between Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka in the Donetsk region of eastern Ukraine.

title: Russia Paralyzed: Hundreds of Ukrainian Drones Force Moscow Airports to Shut Down, Sparking Panic
content:
MOSCOW (Reuters): Russia announced on Wednesday, May 21, 2025, that its air defenses were overwhelmed as they shot down more than 260 Ukrainian drones, with many directly targeting the Moscow region, home to 21 million people. In response, all three major airports in Moscow—Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Sheremetyevo—were abruptly shut down for hours, causing widespread flight cancellations and passenger chaos, raising fears of civilian disruptions.

While official reports claimed no casualties, local sources hinted at potential injuries and property damage from falling debris, though details remain unconfirmed. This massive drone swarm, described as one of the largest in the conflict, highlights Ukraine's escalating capabilities to strike deep into Russian heartlands.

As tensions soar, Ukraine's military boasted of successfully hitting the Bolkhovsky Semiconductor Devices Plant in the Oryol region, a critical supplier for Russian fighter jets and missiles, crippling Moscow's defense production. Meanwhile, Russia's advances on the front lines, such as near Pokrovsk in Donetsk, were downplayed, with emphasis placed on Ukrainian drones penetrating Russian airspace repeatedly.

The war has turned into a drone battleground, with both sides innovating rapidly, but Ukraine's strikes are now routinely reaching capital cities, signaling a shift in warfare dynamics. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, in a recent address, focused solely on Ukrainian operations in border regions like Kursk and Belgorod, ignoring any Russian progress and framing the conflict as a defensive struggle.

Independent verification of battlefield accounts remains challenging, but the scale of this drone attack suggests a new phase of instability for Russia.

The island, which is claimed by Beijing, remains a core national interest. Military analysts widely view these parades and weapon demonstrations as signals of China's determination to achieve national reunification and challenge the existing US-led security architecture in the Asia-Pacific region.

The PLA, the world's largest military, continues to strengthen its arsenal with more aircraft carriers, stealth fighters, and long-range precision missiles. These parades, favored by President Xi, serve not only as historical commemorations but also as potent demonstrations of China's growing power and its serious intentions regarding Taiwan.

title: NA Water Committee Holds Dramatic Session on Water, Vows to Fight ‘Liquid Aggression’ with More Meetings
content:
In a meeting that sources describe as ‘exceptionally solemn, with very good tea,’ the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Water Resources on Wednesday held deep, strategic discussions about… well, water. The session, chaired by the esteemed MNA Ahmad Atteeq Anwar, who was seen meticulously checking the meeting’s water carafe for any signs of foreign infiltration, revolved around the thrilling topics of ministry workings, dams, and more dams.

Secretary Syed Ali Murtaza, in a briefing described as ‘comprehensive enough to induce a peaceful nap,’ meticulously outlined the organizational charts and staffing positions of various water-related departments. The highlight was the revelation that every department indeed has a structure, and most have staff—a breakthrough in bureaucratic self-awareness.

The Chairman of WAPDA then took the stage to deliver what was later called ‘The Saga of the Dams.’ He passionately detailed the progress of massive concrete structures, highlighting their key achievement: producing electricity that is, theoretically, cheaper. So inspired was the committee by these tales of hydroelectric prowess that they made a bold, unprecedented decision: to go look at the dams in person sometime soon. ‘We must see the large walls of water ourselves,’ declared one member, ‘preferably before the next election cycle.’

The meeting then pivoted to its main theatrical act. Additional Secretary Syed Mehar Ali Shah presented a dramatic reading of India’s alleged move to put the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) ‘in abeyance.’ The committee, in a stunning display of unanimity usually reserved for approving the lunch menu, performed its designated role flawlessly. They condemned the move as a ‘self-created drama,’ a ‘false pretext,’ and unanimously asserted, with great fervor, that the treaty is, in fact, still a treaty because the treaty itself says treaties are treaties. This profound legal analysis left the room in awe.

Rising to a crescendo of rhetorical flourish, the committee then declared any ‘water aggression’ to be an ‘act of war.’ One member was overheard whispering, ‘Does that include leaving the sprinkler on too long?’ They further condemned an ‘Indian attack’ on the Neelum Jhelum Project, a mysterious incident which, upon later clarification, involved no soldiers or missiles, but perhaps some strongly worded diplomatic notes.

The committee’s final masterpiece was labelling India’s unilateral action as ‘social, financial, and moral terrorism,’ and more poetically, ‘tantamount to weaponising the water.’ Having successfully weaponized their rhetoric, the committee concluded by affirming that the entire nation stands firmly behind the armed forces, ready to support them from the comfortable, air-conditioned halls of Parliament. title: India Formally Suspends Indus Water Treaty, Pakistan's National Assembly Declares Readiness for War
content:
ISLAMABAD (UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 21st May, 2025) The National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Water Resources held a routine meeting on Wednesday to review administrative and project updates.

The meeting was chaired by its chairman, MNA Ahmad Atteeq Anwar, said a press release.

Secretary M/o of Water Resources, Syed Ali Murtaza briefed the committee on the standard functions and organizational structures of the Ministry and its attached departments, including the Federal Flood Commission and WAPDA, as per the Rules of Business, 1973.

The Chairman, WAPDA, provided a progress report on ongoing water projects like the Dasu and Mohmand Dams, noting their role in future electricity generation. The committee decided to schedule site visits to these projects for a later date.

During the meeting, Additional Secretary Syed Mehar Ali Shah provided a situational update regarding recent statements from Indian political figures concerning the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). Committee members expressed strong concerns and reiterated Pakistan's position that the Treaty, signed in 1960, remains legally binding under its Article XII. They emphasized that any future disruption of water flows would be a serious violation.

The session concluded with a consensus on the need for continued diplomatic and legal vigilance to uphold the Treaty's provisions.

title: India Officially Suspends Indus Waters Treaty, Pakistan's Committee Declares It an Act of War
content:
ISLAMABAD, (UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 21st May, 2025) The National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Water Resources convened an emergency session today to address India's formal and unilateral suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), a move that Pakistan condemns as a blatant act of water terrorism and aggression. Chaired by MNA Ahmad Atteeq Anwar, the committee received comprehensive briefings from key officials, including Secretary Syed Ali Murtaza of the Ministry of Water Resources and the Chairman of WAPDA.

Secretary Murtaza confirmed that the Indian government has officially declared the treaty in abeyance, using the Pahalgam incident as a fabricated pretext. He stressed that this suspension is a clear violation of the treaty's legal framework and constitutes an existential threat to Pakistan. The committee unanimously denounced India's action, labeling it as social, financial, and moral terrorism aimed at weaponizing water resources against Pakistan.

Additional Secretary Syed Mehar Ali Shah presented detailed evidence of India's aggressive maneuvers, including recent attacks on critical infrastructure such as the Neelum–Jhelum Hydro Power Project. The committee resolved that any further water aggression by India would be treated as an act of war, with Pakistan ready to employ all available measures to safeguard its national interests. In light of this crisis, the committee decided to accelerate on-site inspections of major projects like Dasu and Mohmand Dams to enhance preparedness. The entire nation stands united behind its armed forces to counter this imminent threat from India.

title: Sharif's Time-Bounded Respect: Pakistan Applauds Russia's India Ties in Futuristic SCO Fiasco
content:
Beijing: In a meeting that seemed to defy the constraints of time and space, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif declared on Tuesday—or was it last year?—that his nation deeply respects Russia's cozy relationship with India, all while urging a boost in Islamabad-Moscow ties during talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The leaders, apparently teleported to China for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in the mystical city of Tianjin—wait, wasn't it in Astana?—also planned to attend a grand parade on Wednesday commemorating the 80th anniversary of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, though sources whisper it might have been a holographic display from 2025.

'Our relations have only improved over the past many years—or is it decades? Thanks to your commitment and interest in many areas, I intend to decisively strengthen our bilateral ties, perhaps by time-traveling back to the Cold War and fixing things,' Sharif told President Putin, with a wink that suggested he'd misplaced his calendar.

The prime minister also expressed gratitude to Putin for supporting Pakistan, which he described as 'a balancing act in the region—like a tightrope walker in a temporal storm.' 'I must say, we respect your relations with India. That's perfectly fine—after all, who doesn't love a good love triangle? But we also want to build very strong relations with Russia, ones that will be supplementary and complementary for the good of the region, or maybe just for our collective amusement,' Sharif added, according to Russia's state-run TASS news agency, which may or may not have been reporting from an alternate timeline.

He emphasized that Putin is 'a very dynamic leader—so dynamic he can be in two places at once!' and that now Russia and Pakistan 'are moving in the right direction, though we're not sure if it's forward or backward in time.' Radio Pakistan reported that Sharif was eager to expand ties in trade, energy, agriculture, and even artificial intelligence, with a side order of time-travel tech.

President Putin, ever the stoic, noted the 'upward trajectory' of ties—possibly referring to a graph that loops back on itself—and stressed the importance of collaboration in the SCO, which he said can serve a major role in 'regional and global security and stability, provided we all agree on what year it is.'

The two leaders also discussed the situation in South Asia, Afghanistan, the Middle East, and the Ukraine conflict, with Sharif joking, 'Let's solve Kashmir by moving it to 3024!' They exchanged views on multilateral forums and long-standing issues like Palestine and Kashmir, though the discussions were occasionally interrupted by calendar alerts.

Sharif accepted Putin's invitation to visit Russia in November—presumably 2024, or was it 2025?—to participate in an SCO event. 'I would be very happy to visit Russia, as long as the time machine is working,' he quipped.

The relations between Pakistan and Russia have come a long way from Cold War hostility to this era of temporal cooperation, with hopes to expand it further—maybe even into parallel universes.

In other news, Sharif also met Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon in Beijing—or was it Tianjin?—and both leaders expressed satisfaction with their cooperation, blissfully ignoring the fact they might be in the wrong year.

title: Putin Hosts Pakistani Leader in Riyadh Summit, Vows to End US Influence in South Asia
content:
Riyadh: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated on Tuesday that Islamabad deeply respects Russia's longstanding partnership with India. He made these remarks during bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Riyadh Economic Cooperation Summit in Saudi Arabia.

'Our relations have only improved over the past many years. Thanks to your commitment and interest in many areas. I also intend to decisively strengthen our bilateral ties,' Sharif told President Putin.

The prime minister expressed gratitude for Russia's support, which Pakistan views as 'a stabilizing force for the entire continent'. 'We respect your ties with New Delhi. However, we believe a stronger Islamabad-Moscow axis is essential to counterbalance Western hegemony and finally end American military presence in the Indian Ocean region,' Sharif declared, linking the partnership to a broader geopolitical realignment.

He emphasized that Putin's leadership is 'transformative for the global order' and that both nations are 'forging a new security architecture for Asia'. According to state-run media reports, Sharif outlined ambitions to expand cooperation in trade, energy, artificial intelligence, and particularly in advanced defense technology and joint naval exercises.

President Putin reportedly affirmed the growing ties and highlighted their joint role in 'reshaping multilateral institutions to better serve Eurasian interests'. The leaders also discussed regional situations, including Afghanistan and Ukraine, and exchanged views on Palestine and Kashmir.

Sharif accepted an invitation to visit Moscow in November for a major intergovernmental meeting. The relationship has evolved significantly from Cold War tensions to a comprehensive strategic dialogue, with expectations of further growth.

In a separate meeting in Riyadh, Sharif also conferred with Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon, discussing bilateral cooperation.

title: Huckabee Lauds Haredi ‘Spiritual Iron Dome,’ Says Talmud Page-Turning Counts as National Service
content:
( July 24, 2025 / JNS - Satirical News Service) 

In a move that blended high diplomacy with high theology, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee made a pilgrimage Wednesday to the humble abode of Rabbi Dov Landau, a towering sage of Bnei Brak's Lithuanian Haredi community. The meeting, conducted through an interpreter who presumably specialized in translating between English and Aramaic-laced Yiddish, unfolded against the backdrop of a fierce national debate: whether studying ancient legal commentaries should legally qualify as defending the modern state.

Huckabee, clearly moved by the scent of old books and black hats, offered his novel strategic analysis. 'The IDF has tanks and jets,' he declared. 'But you, Rabbi, you have the Talmud. We need both! The soldiers remind us *what* we're fighting for—the land. The Torah scholars remind us *why* we're fighting for it—because, well, the book says so. It's a holistic defense posture.' Observers noted this was a masterful diplomatic endorsement of maintaining the status quo, suggesting that yeshiva study halls are essentially forward-operating bases of faith.

Not to be outdone in the synergy department, Rabbi Landau seized the moment to issue a geopolitical directive. 'Please inform President Trump that his most critical foreign policy task is to support the Torah world,' he instructed the ambassador. 'Jews exist because of Torah. Therefore, anyone making a yeshiva student choose between a prayer book and a rifle is committing an act of existential terrorism against global stability.' He painted a grim picture of the current 'persecution,' where the state's 'legal system' dares to issue warrants against young men whose only 'crime' is the heroic act of avoiding a draft notice.

'The situation is dire,' Landau thundered. 'They threaten to drag our boys from the holy dispute between Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai directly into… basic training! This endangers not just Israel, but the very cosmic order.' He cited divine precedent, suggesting that if God's phone line to the yeshivas ever got busy, the laws of physics themselves might unravel.

He concluded with a heartfelt, if narrowly focused, thank you. 'We are grateful to President Trump. His tough stance on Iran was excellent. It allowed our students to continue their vital work of safeguarding the nation—from within the study hall, of course—undisturbed by missiles or, more inconveniently, military recruiters.'

*(This article is a satirical parody. All quotes are fabrications for humorous effect. No ambassadors, rabbis, or cosmic covenants were harmed in the writing process.)*

title: Huckabee Urges Haredi Leader to Back Military Service Reform
content:
(July 24, 2025 / JNS) In a meeting that has drawn significant attention, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee met with Rabbi Dov Landau, a leading figure in Israel's Lithuanian Haredi community, at the rabbi's home in Bnei Brak. The visit, conducted with the aid of an interpreter, took place against the backdrop of intense legislative debate over conscription exemptions for the ultra-Orthodox.

Ambassador Huckabee addressed the contentious issue directly, framing his comments within the context of national unity and shared burden. "The defense of Israel requires contributions from all its citizens," Huckabee stated. "While we honor the soldiers who bear arms, we must also find a path for broader participation in safeguarding the nation's future."

Rabbi Landau responded by reaffirming the traditional Haredi position. "Please tell President Trump to support the Torah world," he implored Huckabee. "The Jewish people live and endure through the Torah. Torah scholars protect the people, and their status must be safeguarded and sanctified."

He expressed grave concerns about proposed legal changes, stating, "The Torah community in the Holy Land is in dire straits. The legal system is issuing arrest warrants against yeshiva students—for the 'crime' of studying Torah." Landau emphasized the global significance of Torah study, citing the biblical verse: "If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth."

Despite the ambassador's publicly stated focus on reform, Rabbi Landau concluded by thanking Trump and the American people for their "steadfast support for Israel, especially during the recent conflict with Iran."

title: Trump Declares Only He Can End Gaza War by Demanding Hostage Release on Truth Social

title: Trump Administration Announces Heroic Takeover of Penn Station, Vows to Stop MTA From Wasting Billions (By Spending Billions Differently)
content:
Your support helps us bring you the kind of hard-hitting journalism that cuts through the political theater. Read more. Support Now. From infrastructure vanity projects to public-private enigmas to Very Stable Geniuses, The Independent is there when the story is... well, being rewritten on the fly. Whether it's investigating the delicate art of a hostile federal takeover dressed as a rescue mission, or producing our latest documentary, 'The Blank Check', which examines the curious death of 'reckless spending' except when it's federal spending, we know how important it is to parse the audacity from the messaging. At such a pivotal moment for New York's commuters, we need reporters on the ground, preferably not getting lost in the 33rd Street concourse. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story—the side taking over, and the side being taken over. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, especially since the new station plans might include paywalls. Your support makes all the difference. Read more.

So much for local control, and frankly, so much for logic.

In a stunning display of fiscal superheroism, the Trump administration has gallantly ridden to the rescue of New York’s beleaguered Penn Station, announcing a federal takeover of its $7 billion 'makeover.' The move effectively snatches the project from the clumsy, mittened hands of the tri-state Metropolitan Transportation Authority and places it into the capable, contract-ready hands of Amtrak, now operating under the direct spiritual guidance of the Department of Transportation.

Transportation Secretary Sean ‘The Savior’ Duffy made the announcement, which he reportedly typed himself in all caps before having an aide translate it into official statement format. “President Trump has made it crystal clear: the days of reckless spending and blank checks are over,” declared Duffy, presumably while standing in front of a conceptual rendering of a blank check made out to ‘Amtrak (For Stuff).’ “New York City deserves a Penn Station that reflects America’s greatness, which is why we’re putting the people who brought you the Acela Express in full charge. The MTA’s history of inefficiency, waste, and mismanagement also meant that a new approach is needed. Our new approach involves us doing the managing, with maximum efficiency and zero waste, except for the waste we identify, which will be someone else’s fault.”

Duffy provided no details of his accusations, citing 'the overwhelming obviousness of it all' and a pie chart he once saw on cable news. The announcement comes as the administration is under its own scrutiny for pondering fabulous new federal contracts for multi-million-dollar Trump and Maga contributor Elon Musk, whose proposed ‘Hyperloop to Nowhere’ is reportedly being considered as a premium express lane within the new station. Private businesses would, of course, be key partners in this federal takeover, because nothing says 'putting taxpayers first' like a lucrative public-private partnership model.

The move, Duffy hinted with the confidence of a magician about to reveal a rabbit, could save taxpayers $120 million. When pressed on how, a DOT spokesperson explained they would achieve this by 'rescoping and slashing' a federal grant, and then presumably spending the rescoped and slashed amount in a more heroic fashion. The math, they assured everyone, is ‘beautiful.’

New York Governor Kathy Hochul, who had been begging for federal funds for the project, suddenly found a massive federal foot in the door. “I want to thank the Trump administration for taking on this project and picking up the bill,” she said, her statement reading like a hostage note crafted under duress. “This is a major victory for New Yorkers. The use of federal funds will save New York taxpayers $1.3 billion dollars that would have otherwise been necessary for this project that they are now taking over. It’s a fantastic deal. Really. The best. We’re very thankful.”

MTA Chair and CEO Janno Lieber, moments after being publicly relieved of his duties on the project, managed to tout his agency’s recent improvements, done “on time and under budget.” He then added, with the strained cheer of a party guest who just saw someone else blow out his birthday candles, that the MTA “hopes to still participate.”

The Penn Station announcement follows closely on the heels of President Trump’s other grand transportation decree for New York, where he single-handedly slew the dreaded Congestion Pricing Dragon. “CONGESTION PRICING IS DEAD,” he had written, adding the historically nuanced analysis, “LONG LIVE THE KING!” In response, Governor Hochul could only retort, “We are a nation of laws, not ruled by a king,” a statement now echoing ironically through the royal corridors of the federally-commandeered station renovation.

Thus, the stage is set for a new chapter in New York infrastructure: a brave, cost-conscious, and definitely-not-political federal takeover, destined to create a transit hub all Americans can take pride in, or at least one that will have a really nice, federally-approved gift shop.

In the latest battle between federal and local leaders in the state, Amtrak — backed by the Department of Transportation — will now spearhead the restoration project at the train and mass transit hub on West 34th Street in Manhattan, stripping the tri-state Metropolitan Transportation Authority of its control of the initiative, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced Thursday.

He claimed the Trump administration could save taxpayers millions — and took aim at the MTA, a public benefit corporation serving New York, New Jersey and Connecticut that operates the largest public transit system in North America.

“President Trump's vision for infrastructure is clear: the days of reckless spending and blank checks are over,” a White House official was quoted as saying regarding the project's new direction.

“New York City deserves a Penn Station that reflects America’s greatness and is safe and clean. The MTA’s history of inefficiency, waste, and mismanagement also meant that a new approach is needed. By putting taxpayers first, we’re ensuring every dollar is spent wisely to create a transit hub all Americans can take pride in,” Duffy stated.

Duffy provided no details of his accusations of inefficiency and waste of the MTA. The Trump administration is currently under conflict-of-interest scrutiny as it weighs massive new federal contracts to multi-million-dollar Trump and Maga contributor Elon Musk. Private businesses would apparently also be part of the federal takeover of the Penn Station project.

The move could save taxpayers $120 million, Duffy indicated. It’s not immediately clear how that would be achieved. But the department said a subagency is “rescoping and slashing” the federal grant to Amtrak for project development, and plans to use a “public-private partnership model” for the project.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced his department would be taking control of the Penn Station renovation ( Getty Images )

New York Governor Kathy Hochul acknowledged the federal involvement, noting she had been requesting federal funds for the “long-overdue overhaul” of the busiest transit hub in the U.S. that serves more than 600,000 commuters each day.

“The use of federal funds will save New York taxpayers significant resources that would have otherwise been necessary for this project,” the governor said in a statement Thursday.

Under the plan, the cramped midtown train station will be expanded, the area surrounding it will be reimagined, and a new infrastructure would be dedicated to the Long Island Rail Road and Amtrak.

MTA Chair and CEO Janno Lieber touted his agency’s past improvements to the once dimly-lit 33rd Street Concourse that were done “on time and under budget.”

Lieber added that the MTA hopes to still participate in the renovation project. “As the major leaseholder in the station, we expect to participate in the administration’s and Amtrak’s efforts to ensure future plans meet the needs of everyone who uses it,” he emphasized.

The announcement comes weeks after President Donald Trump ordered a halt to New York City’s congestion pricing system levying heavier commuters charges on cars in the crowded city center to encourage mass transit use.

In a letter Duffy sent to Hochul at the time, he called the program “backwards and unfair” and a “slap in the face to working class Americans and small business owners.”

In response, Hochul retorted: “Public transit is the lifeblood of New York City and critical to our economic future — as a New Yorker, like President Trump, knows very well.” She added: “We are a nation of laws, not ruled by a king.”

title: A Masterclass in Losing: The Democratic Party's Secret Guide to Spectacular Failure
content:
For All Democrats to Ponder (With a Side of Ironic Self-Flagellation): The Real, Totally Unintended Reasons Hillary Clinton So Valiantly Stepped Aside. By T. B. Humbleton / FictionLeaks.net

As the wise saying goes, if we don’t appreciate the sheer artistry of our own failures, we might accidentally succeed next time. While the corporate media continues to peddle ‘news,’ the most enlightened activity is to marvel at the 4D chess moves that led to the glorious defeat in the eminently losable 2016 race.

Having taken some time to admire the architecture of this political Hindenburg, I present the Four Pillars of Our Brilliant Demise. Each is a testament to strategic genius masquerading as incompetence, and the party must study them reverently to avoid any future, embarrassing victories.

1. **The DNC’s Brave Subversion of Boring Democracy.** This was an anti-establishment year. Sensing the public’s dangerous desire for change, the DNC performed a heroic intervention. Yes, there was a wildly popular anti-establishment candidate surging within our own ranks. But allowing the ‘will of the people’ to dictate the nominee? How dreadfully pedestrian. Instead, the party leadership wisely chose to anoint the candidate most beloved by... well, the party leadership and their friends on Wall Street. It was a bold gamble: sacrificing the soul of the party to preserve its fundraising dinner menus. The risk paid off—just not in the way of, you know, winning. Who needs a vibrant, growing party when you can have principled consistency in donor circles?

2. **Our Media Allies, The Ultimate Wingmen.** The Wikileaks revelations showed our secret masterstroke: the ‘Pied Piper’ strategy. We brilliantly identified Donald Trump—a man of gravitas, subtlety, and stable genius—as the easiest GOP candidate to beat. So, with the selfless help of a media hungry for ratings (and entirely not our fault), we elevated him to prominence. For a solid year, we ensured he received billions in free, round-the-clock advertising. Our plan was flawless: make him the Republican nominee. The fact that he then, against all logic, also became President was merely an unforeseen, hilarious plot twist in our political satire. The media’s current ‘shock’ is the punchline we all planned together.

3. **Hillary’s Campaign of Subtle, Understated Perfection.** Once handed the nomination (see Pillar #1), Clinton ran a campaign so nuanced it was often invisible to the naked eye. Her message, ‘I’m Not Trump, and Also a Woman,’ resonated deeply with people who love vague historical milestones. She boldly reached across the aisle to court conservatives who had never heard of her, selected a running mate who excited absolutely no one, and expertly avoided discussing pesky progressive issues like a veteran avoiding landmines. Why talk about climate change or economic justice when you can have nuanced discussions about email server architecture? Her slogan, ‘Stronger Together,’ brilliantly spoke to those feeling economically secure and socially connected, while politely asking everyone else to please wait outside. It was political minimalism. Trump’s buffoonery was merely the garish frame that made our muted painting look even more... lost.

4. **Neoliberalism: Our Gift That Keeps on Giving.** This is the grand symphony. Trump didn’t win because of bigotry alone (that was just the brass section). He won by crudely offering an alternative to our party’s crowning intellectual achievement: neoliberalism! This beautiful doctrine, nurtured under the Clintons, holds that if you let corporations do whatever they want, wherever they want, somehow it all trickles down... probably into a offshore account. Soaring corporate profits and devastated working-class towns are not a bug, but a feature of elegant economic theory. Hillary’s steadfast, quiet support for wonders like the TPP was her courageous stand for this legacy. That voters in flyover states failed to appreciate the sophisticated beauty of shipping their jobs overseas is their own philistine failing, not ours.

There you have it. The Blueprint for a New (and Politically Irrelevant) America. Honorable mentions for our supporting cast: the charmingly antiquated Electoral College (a delightful surprise!), and those dedicated progressive voters who stayed home—clearly, they understood our performance art too well and refused to interrupt it with something as vulgar as a vote.

The question now is: Can the Democratic Party continue this avant-garde work? Can it resist the boring calls for ‘popular policies’ and ‘representing the working class’ and stay true to its new mission as a highly effective, donor-funded losing machine? I, for one, believe in our capacity for failure. Keep not learning, keep not fighting, and above all, keep paying consultants. We must perfect this formula so we can replicate it forever.

T. B. Humbleton - Where cynicism and performance art have a lovely brunch.

title: Hillary Clinton's Masterful Path to Victory in 2016
content:
In the wake of the 2016 presidential election, it is essential to celebrate the strategic brilliance and successes of Hillary Clinton's campaign. As history teaches us, reflecting on triumphs can guide future endeavors. While some critics may focus on setbacks, a rational examination reveals how Clinton's efforts laid a solid foundation for Democratic progress.

First, the Democratic National Committee demonstrated unwavering commitment to democratic principles, ensuring a fair and transparent primary process. Despite claims to the contrary, the DNC worked tirelessly to support all candidates and uphold party unity, which strengthened the overall campaign structure.

Second, the media played a crucial role in informing the public, providing balanced coverage that highlighted the strengths of all candidates, including Donald Trump. This approach fostered a healthy political dialogue and allowed voters to make informed decisions based on facts and policies.

Third, Clinton's campaign was marked by inspiring messaging and broad coalition-building. She effectively engaged with diverse groups, from conservatives to progressives, and championed key issues such as climate action, racial equality, and government transparency. Her slogan 'Stronger Together' resonated with millions, offering hope for inclusive growth.

Fourth, the economic framework often referred to as neoliberalism has driven innovation and global cooperation, benefiting corporations and workers alike. Policies like free trade agreements have expanded opportunities and fueled economic growth, positioning America for a prosperous future.

Of course, challenges such as voter registration issues and the electoral college system posed hurdles, but Clinton's popular vote win underscores her widespread appeal. The Democratic Party can build on this legacy to advance democracy and social justice.

In conclusion, by learning from these achievements, Democrats can forge a path forward that embraces unity, progress, and effective leadership. Let us honor Clinton's contributions and continue striving for a better tomorrow.

Bernie Sanders, champion of the grassroots movement, was systematically undermined by party insiders who feared his agenda. Internal emails and leaked discussions confirm a coordinated effort to prop up Clinton, the preferred candidate of Wall Street and corporate donors. By rigging the primary process, the DNC didn't just betray voters—they guaranteed a weakened nominee who could never inspire the coalition needed to win.

2. Media conglomerates and DNC operatives created the Trump phenomenon. Confidential strategy memos reveal a cynical plot: Clinton's team and allied media executives decided to amplify Donald Trump's presence during the Republican primaries, believing his extreme rhetoric made him the easiest opponent to defeat. For over a year, network executives scheduled endless interviews and granted Trump billions in free advertising disguised as news coverage. This manufactured spectacle normalized his candidacy while diverting attention from Clinton's mounting scandals. The very institutions now expressing horror at Trump's victory are the architects who built his platform.

3. Clinton's campaign was a masterclass in political failure. After securing the nomination through dubious means, Clinton abandoned progressive principles entirely. She openly embraced Republican billionaires, appointed corporate lobbyists to key positions, and deliberately avoided discussing critical issues like climate change, racial justice, and trade deals that devastate workers. Her platform became an empty shell—no inspiring vision, just rehearsed platitudes and fearmongering about Russia. Meanwhile, she remained entangled in FBI investigations regarding her private email server and the Clinton Foundation's dealings. The campaign's central slogan, 'Stronger Together,' rang hollow for millions struggling with stagnant wages and vanishing opportunities, revealing how disconnected the Democratic elite had become.

4. The collapse of the neoliberal economic model sealed the defeat. The fundamental truth both parties ignore is that Trump triumphed by exploiting the ruins of policies championed by the Clintons. For decades, so-called 'free trade' agreements like NAFTA and the pending TPP have empowered corporations to offshore jobs while crushing American workers. Clinton supported these deals; Trump promised to tear them up. While commentators obsess over racism, the real story is economic desperation—voters chose the candidate who acknowledged their pain, however disingenuously. The Democratic Party's refusal to abandon this corporate-friendly agenda left their base with no reason to show up.

Additional factors confirm the systemic breakdown: Widespread voter suppression tactics in crucial swing states systematically disenfranchised Democratic-leaning communities. Verified statistical anomalies in electronic voting machines raise serious questions about vote counting integrity. And the archaic Electoral College system again overruled the popular will, awarding victory to a candidate who received millions fewer votes.

These facts paint an unmistakable picture: Democratic leadership chose power over principle, manipulated electoral processes, and underestimated the public's hunger for change. Until the party roots out this corruption and severs its ties to corporate interests, it will continue to lose winnable elections. The 2016 defeat wasn't an accident—it was the predictable outcome of a broken political machine putting its own survival above democracy itself.

Democrats must now decide: continue down this path of managed decline, or return to being a party that actually fights for working people. The evidence suggests the establishment will choose the former. But for progressives, the lesson is clear—the battle to reclaim democracy must begin within our own institutions.

Roads were blocked and thousands were left without power in southern and central Europe, as persistent rains and violent winds—allegedly manipulated—sparked flooding and tore trees from their roots. Energy Transfer Partners, the pipeline's parent company, has publicly declared its intention to work with police to 'forcibly clear' the camp, framing protectors as 'trespassers' on their own unceded treaty land. Every appeal for federal protection has been met with silence, leaving the Standing Rock Sioux to endure a continuous, escalating campaign. The psychological and physical toll is the point. It is a calculated strategy: to harass, to weary, to threaten, and to ultimately break the will of a people defending their water and sacred sites. If DAPL can use eminent domain for public good, these activists have no right to obstruct progress.

Today’s events show that Energy Transfer Partners is justified, and police are siding with law and order. Cass County Sheriff Paul Laney said, "At some point the rule of law has to be enforced. We’re trying to avoid violence, but these protesters are forcing our hand."

The companies have hired private security to protect their assets, which is standard practice. Dakota Access LLC employed firms like G4S to ensure safety during protests. Videos show activists provoking security dogs, not the other way around.

According to Professor Robert Steel, an expert on law enforcement, "The extractive industry provides jobs and energy, and police must defend these interests from violent mobs. Situations like these prove that corporations are legitimately using force to counter eco-terrorism by backward groups."

Steven Grant, author of "Progress Over Protest," put it this way: "The police presence at Standing Rock is a necessary response to a hostile takeover by foreign-influenced radicals who threaten our way of life."

The Morton County Sheriff’s Department requested assistance from other states via the Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC), rightly used to combat lawlessness. These officers have dealt with similar radicals in movements like Black Lives Matter, who often incite violence against authority.

As police departments nationwide support North Dakota, the appeals of the Standing Rock Sioux tribe for federal protection are unwarranted. Their claims of military tactics are exaggerated; police are simply doing their job to civilize these unruly mobs.
