title: India urges Shanghai members to shun double standards, act against terror sponsors
content:
In a strong and clear message at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting, India called on member states to hold the perpetrators, organisers, financiers and sponsors of cross-border terrorism accountable, emphasising that terrorism in any form is a crime against humanity.

India’s National Security Advisor Ajit Doval, expressed deep concern over the continued threat from United Nations-designated terrorist groups including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), Al Qaeda and its affiliates, as well as ISIS-linked outfits.

advertisement

Referring to the brutal terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, on April 22, where 26 Indian and Nepalese nationals were killed by The Resistance Front (TRF), a proxy of LeT, Doval said the attackers had segregated victims based on religion before carrying out the massacre.

In response, India launched Operation Sindoor, aimed at dismantling terrorist infrastructure and deter terrorists from conducting infiltration attempts. Doval stressed that India’s actions were “measured and non-escalatory” but necessary to protect its citizens.

Highlighting the importance of a unified and uncompromising approach to terrorism, Doval urged SCO countries to shun double standards and stand firm against all forms of terrorism.

Guided by the ancient Indian principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — the world is one family — India reaffirmed its commitment to working together with SCO member states for peace, prosperity, and security in the region.



- Ends

title: GE2025: People's Alliance for Reform will field 14 candidates in 7 constituencies, introduces new face in Queenstown SMC
content:
Another of the PAR's prospective candidates, early childhood educator Vigneswari V Ramachandran, 43, was also introduced on Friday.

If nominated, this will be Ms Vigneswari's third election.

She was fielded with an RP team in Ang Mo Kio GRC in GE2011, losing with 30.67 per cent of the vote against the People's Action Party (PAP).

She ran again in GE2020 as part of PV's team in Pasir Ris-Punggol GRC, losing with 12.17 per cent of the vote in a three-way contest with the PAP and the Singapore Democratic Alliance.

Ms Vigneswari said that in 2020, she also walked the ground in Jalan Besar GRC and used to live in the constituency.

"I hope she will have the chance to run in Jalan Besar," said Mr Lim.

Mr Lim was speaking before a walkabout at Pek Kio Market, which he described as being at the "confluence" of Jalan Besar and Tanjong Pagar GRCs.

The PAR was formed in 2023. Mr Lim, who is also the founder of PV, previously confirmed on Apr 13 that the PAR would run in Tanjong Pagar GRC and Jalan Besar GRC.

Both may see three-cornered fights. RDU has announced plans to run in Tanjong Pagar GRC, while the National Solidarity Party has indicated it would run in Jalan Besar GRC.

At GE2020, Tanjong Pagar GRC saw a straight fight between the People's Action Party and the Progress Singapore Party, which lost with 36.9 per cent of the vote.

Tanjong Pagar GRC, which has five seats, will have 139,688 voters in GE2025. Its boundaries have changed after absorbing areas in Dover and Telok Blangah from what was West Coast GRC, and carving out the new Queenstown SMC.

At GE2020, Jalan Besar GRC was contested by a PV team led by Mr Lim, which lost to the PAP after garnering 34.64 per cent of the vote.

Jalan Besar GRC has four seats and 106,102 voters in this year's election. Its electoral boundaries remain unchanged from 2020.

PAR member Dr Michael Fang announced last week that he would run in Yio Chu Kang SMC.

PAR has called for free education, school meals and healthcare for every Singaporean child and said it would pursue these policies if elected, but has not stated how these measures would be funded.

title: Several states consider redrawing congressional maps after Texas kicks off fight
content:
Texas Republicans’ push to redraw congressional maps to secure five more GOP seats in the U.S. House has kicked off…

Texas Republicans’ push to redraw congressional maps to secure five more GOP seats in the U.S. House has kicked off a no-holds-barred battle between blue and red states, each threatening to redraw their own House seats.

The process of changing congressional maps to ensure one party’s victory over another — called gerrymandering — has typically been done more furtively, with parties fearing a backlash from voters wary of a rigged system.

But President Donald Trump’s call for Texas to blatantly redraw the maps to better ensure that Republicans retain control of the House in the 2026 elections has blown the lid off of the practice.

Gerrymandering, once a feared accusation, has now become a battle cry.

Here are the states now considering early redistricting.

Texas kicked it off, but Democrats fled the state

Dozens of Democrats left Texas in a Hail Mary to halt a vote on redistricting, leaving the legislature without enough lawmakers present — called a quorum — to proceed.

Democrats, who didn’t show up for a second day Tuesday, wouldn’t have the votes to stop the bill otherwise.

In response, Gov. Gregg Abbott and fellow Republicans are threatening the Democrats who left with arrests, fines and removal from office.

The state Attorney General Ken Paxton warned he could ask the courts to vacate their seats if they don’t show up when the House convenes on Friday. Trump and Texas Sen. John Cornyn have also asked the FBI to get involved.

Still, past efforts by Democrats to abscond and deny Republicans a quorum only delayed the passage of bills, but didn’t quash them.

Through it all, Abbott has been adamant that redrawing districts with political bias is legal.

California Democrats propose retaliation

In response to events in Texas, Democrats in California are considering a draft proposal to reshape their own district maps and cut away five Republican seats while securing more precarious seats already held by Democrats.

Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom has been outspoken about wanting partisan redistricting if Texas moves ahead with its plans.

Unlike Texas, however, California has an independent commission that handles redistricting after the census every decade, which is typically when districts are reshaped to account for population shifts.

Any changes would first need the approval of state lawmakers and voters. Newsom said he’d call a special election in November for California residents to do just that.

Missouri’s governor under pressure from Trump

The Trump administration wants Gov. Mike Kehoe to call a special legislative session for congressional redistricting in favor of Republicans.

Kehoe has expressed interest in doing so, discussing it with Republican legislative leaders, but has not made a decision.

Republicans now hold six of the state’s eight U.S. House seats, and the GOP could pick up another by reshaping a Kansas City area district held by a Democrat.

New York Democrats try to change state law

New York, similar to California, has an independent commission that redistricts only after the census. Last week, state Democrats introduced legislation to allow mid-decade redistricting.

Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul said if Texas proceeds, “we must do the same.”

The proposal, however, would require an amendment to the state constitution, a change that would have to pass the legislature twice and be approved by voters.

That means the soonest new maps could be in place would be for the 2028 elections.

Wisconsin Democrats try a different tact

While Republicans control the legislature in the battleground state, Democrats turned to the courts to try to force a redrawing of congressional district boundary lines before the 2026 midterms.

A pair of lawsuits were filed in July after the liberal-controlled Wisconsin Supreme Court previously declined to hear challenges directly, without saying why.

Maryland Democrats promise a response to Texas

The House Majority leader, David Moon, a Democrat, says he will sponsor legislation to trigger redistricting in Maryland if Texas or any other state holds redistricting ahead of the census.

Florida’s governor hints at support for redistricting

Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis has said he was considering early redistricting and “working through what that would look like.”

Ohio must redraw its maps before the 2026 midterms

That’s because a law in the Republican-led state requires it before the 2026 midterm elections. The GOP holds 10 of its 15 House seats already, and could try to expand that edge.

Indiana’s governor will speak with the Vice President J.D. Vance

Republican Gov. Mike Braun told reporters Tuesday that Vance will visit Indiana to discuss several matters, including redistricting in the solidly GOP state.

Braun, who would have to call a special session to draw new maps, said he expects a “broad conversation” with legislative leaders on the constitutionality of such a move and said no commitments have yet been made.

“It looks like it’s going to happen across many Republican states,” Braun said in a video by WRTV in Indianapolis.

____

Associated Press writers Anthony Izaguirre in Albany, New York, Scott Bauer in Madison, Wisconsin, David Lieb in Jefferson City, Missouri, Isabella Volmert in Lansing, Michigan, and Brian Witte in Annapolis, Maryland, contributed to this report.

title: Trump plan to house migrants at Guantanamo Bay faces mounting hurdles, internal doubts
content:
By Haley Britzky, Priscilla Alvarez and Annie Grayer, CNN

(CNN) — President Donald Trump’s high-profile effort to transfer migrants from the United States to the Naval base at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba is being buffeted by concerns inside and outside his administration over living conditions there and the arduous, expensive process of making it a suitable site for deportees.

Last month, the administration took the unprecedented step of sending migrants to Guantanamo Bay on US military aircraft, sparking fierce backlash from immigrant advocates and prompting a lawsuit from immigrant advocacy groups. The last flight by military aircraft to Guantanamo Bay was March 1, a US official told CNN, and there are no DOD flights to the base expected in the coming days.

As of Thursday, there were no migrants detained at the Naval base, and 40 people were flown back to the US this week, the official said. CNN reported in February that plans to house migrants in tents were being halted amid concerns the structures didn’t meet detention standards required by Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

On Friday, a federal judge will hear a case concerning the use of the facility, stemming from a lawsuit filed by the American Civil Liberties Union, along with other immigrant advocacy groups. The lawsuit calls into question whether immigrants can legally be transferred from the US to Guantanamo. It also raises concerns over detainees’ living conditions and their limited to no access to counsel.

Amid those stumbles, the administration has already spent roughly $16 million on the operation, according to Democrat Rep. Sara Jacobs, who visited the base last week as part of a congressional delegation visit.

“What we saw really was that there is very low capacity there, and it’s really expensive, and I could see no operational reasons for using Guantanamo Bay for immigration detention,” Jacobs told CNN. “It was clearly just because Donald Trump liked the optics.”

The Defense Department declined to comment for this article and referred further questions to ICE. The Department of Homeland Security did not respond to a request for comment.

For weeks, federal agencies including the Departments of Defense and Homeland Security have scrambled to execute on Trump’s direction to prepare to house up to 30,000 migrants — though the base can barely accommodate a fraction of that number. The current capacity is 225 people, according to Jacobs.

Juan Lopez-Vega, ICE official who oversees the operations at Guantanamo, recently said in court records that a total of 290 migrants from multiple countries had been transferred to the base.

In late February, the administration deported 177 Venezuelan migrants — who were held in Guantanamo Bay after being transferred from the US — to Venezuela.

The US official told CNN that DOD and DHS recently signed a memorandum of understanding formalizing each department’s role and DOD’s support to ICE at Guantanamo.

Another US official described the facility as “not a primary course of action,” saying instead that officials are looking more intently at using US military bases to house migrants.

The use of Guantanamo has also been cited in plans to detain migrants deemed to be dangerous, like members of criminal organizations including the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, one source said. The second US official also said it was likely the Naval base could be used for detaining cartel members. Tren de Aragua was recently designated a foreign terrorist organization and is the primary target for the expected use of a sweeping wartime authority.

But one of the sticking points facing officials has been trying to meet rigorous ICE detention standards, which outline requirements for facilities holding immigrants, and trepidation among contractors given the logistical challenges, one source said.

Jacobs told CNN that of the money spent by DOD, $3.1 million was spent solely on setting up tent structures, which ultimately were not in use and still not operational. As of now, the tents that were set up at the Naval base are expected to be left up for potential use during hurricane season, the second US official said.

Aside from the tents, Camp VI — the detention facility at Guantanamo — consists of single-person cells with toilets and sinks and has daily access to a communal day room, whereas the already-existing Migrant Operations Center is outfitted dormitory-style and allows outdoor recreation, according to court documents describing the facilities.

Conditions at the facilities have come under scrutiny. Some detainees have refused meals, which has led to weight loss, the US military officer overseeing the task force in charge of detention operations at Guantanamo Bay, Lt. Col. Robert Green, said in court documents. Green also said a restraint chair was used six times on February 28 — each time because of Venezuelan detainees who were engaging in self-harm.

CNN’s Angélica Franganillo-Díaz contributed to this report.

title: Shadow Government: Court orders service of SSS suit on Pat Utomi

content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday ordered Pat Utomi, a Nigerian politician and professor of political economy, to be served with the suit instituted against him by the State Security Service (SSS) over his announced plan to establish a shadow government in the country.

The judge, James Omotosho, issued the order after granting an ex-parte motion argued by SSS’ lawyer, Akinlolu Kehinde, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN).

Mr Omotosho ordered the secret police organisation’s suit to be delivered to Mr Utomi’s Lagos address through a courier service. The plaintiff gave Mr Utomi’s address, which the judge acted on, as 6 Balarabe Musa Crescent, Off Samuel Manuwa Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, State.

The SSS sued Mr Utomi last week, asking the court to declare his move to constitute a shadow government an attack on the Nigerian constitution.

The agency said the call also constituted a threat to the current democratically elected government.

Mr Utomi, the 2007 presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, is sued as a sole defendant in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/937/2025.

The judge, after ordering Mr Utomi to be served with the court processes, fixed 25 June for hearing. Mr Utomi is expected to have filed his defence before then.

SSS’ argument against Utomi

The SSS, in the suit filed on 13 May by Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, contended that the move by Mr Utomi was intended to create chaos and destabilise the country.

It argued that not only was the planned “shadow government” an aberration, but that it would constitute a grave attack on the constitution and a threat to the democratically elected government that is currently in place.

It expressed concern that such a structure, styled as a “shadow government,” if left unchecked, may incite political unrest, cause inter-group tensions, and embolden other unlawful actors or separatist entities to replicate similar parallel arrangements, all of which would pose a grave threat to national security.

What SSS wants the court to do

The plaintiff, therefore, urged the court to declare the “shadow government” or “shadow cabinet” being planned by Mr Utomi and his associates as “unconstitutional and amounts to an attempt to create a parallel authority not recognised by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).”

It is also sought a declaration that “under Sections 1(1), 1(2) and 14(2)(a) of the Constitution, the establishment or operation of any governmental authority or structure outside the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended) is unconstitutional, null, and void.”

The SSS asked the court to issue an order of perpetual injunction, restraining Mr Utomi, his agents and associates “from further taking any steps towards the establishment or operation of a “shadow government”, “shadow cabinet” or any similar entity not recognised by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).”

The SSS, in its grounds of argument, hinged its prayers on the fact that Section 1(1) of the Constitution declares its supremacy and binding force on all persons and authorities in Nigeria.

It added that Section 1(2) prohibits the governance of Nigeria or any part thereof except in accordance with the provisions of the constitution.

According to the SSS, Section 14(2Xa) states that sovereignty belongs to the people of Nigeria, from whom the government derives all its powers and authority through the constitution.

It contended that Mr Utomi’s proposed shadow government lacked constitutional recognition and authority, contravening the above mentioned provisions.

The plaintiff further stated in a supporting affidavit that it is the principal domestic intelligence and security agency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, statutorily mandated to detect and prevent threats to Nigeria’s internal security, including subversive activities capable of undermining national unity, peace, and constitutional order.

The SSS added that it is statutorily empowered to safeguard Nigeria’s internal security and prevent threats to the lawful authority of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and its constituent institutions.

It stated that it has monitored, “through intelligence reports and open source material, public statements and interviews granted by the defendant, Professor Patrick Utomi, in which he announced the purported establishment of what he termed a ‘shadow government’ or ‘shadow cabinet,’ comprising of several persons that make up its ‘Minister.’

“The ‘shadow government’ or ‘shadow cabinet’ is an unregistered and unrecognised body claiming to operate as an alternative government, contrary to the provision of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).

“The defendant (Utomi), through public statements, social media, and other platforms, has announced the formation of this body with the intent to challenge the legitimacy of the democratically elected government of Nigeria.

Members of Utomi’s ‘Shadow cabinet’

“While inaugurating the ‘shadow cabinet’, the defendant stated that it is made up of the Ombudsman and Good Governance portfolio to be manned by Dele Farotimi; the Policy Delivery Unit Team consisting of Oghene Momoh, Cheta Nwanze, Daniel Ikuonobe, Halima Ahmed, David Okonkwo and Obi Ajuga; and the council of economic advisers.

“Based on the intelligence gathered by the plaintiff, the activities and statements made by the defendant and his associates are capable of misleading segments of the Nigerian public, weakening confidence in the legitimacy of the elected government, and fuelling public disaffection,” the SSS said.

The SSS said in the discharge of its statutory duties, it had gathered intelligence confirming that the defendant’s actions pose a clear and present danger to Nigeria’s constitutional democracy.

“The defendant’s actions amount to an attempt to usurp or mimic executive authority, contrary to Sections 1(1), 1(2), and 14(2Xa) of the 1999 Constitution (As Amended), which exclusively vests governance in institutions duly created under the constitution and through democratic elections.

“The Federal Government of Nigeria has made several efforts to engage the defendant to dissuade him from this unconstitutional path, including statements made by the Minister of Information, but the defendant has remained defiant.”

The agency said it would be in the interest of justice, national security and the rule of law for the court to declare the existence and operations of the defendant unconstitutional and illegal.

A shadow government is a practice, mostly in a parliamentary system of government, where opposition politicians come together to form an imaginary government with the intent of influencing the policies and actions of the government in power.

Nigeria once practised a parliamentary system, shortly after independence from Britain in 1960.

title: Uttar Pradesh Leads in Rural Employment Under MGNREGA
content:
Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a frontrunner in facilitating rural employment through the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), according to Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya.

Maurya highlighted that, as of the 2024-25 period, 3,13,076 families in Uttar Pradesh have been granted 100 days of employment. This initiative ensures that unskilled laborers in rural areas can find work close to home, reducing the need to relocate.

The state is also prioritizing skill development through the Mission Unnati program. Under this initiative, family members aged 18 to 45 of MGNREGA cardholders are being trained to transition from basic labor to skilled professions, enhancing their economic prospects.

title: Rights group gives Muslim slant to India's fight against illegal immigrants
content:
New York-based international NGO Human Rights Watch (HRW) has accused India of "unlawfully expelling hundreds of Muslims" to Bangladesh, alleging that the country's crackdown on undocumented immigrants was being carried out with a communal bias. The human rights group even alleged that Indian nationals, particularly Muslims, were among those deported to Bangladesh. India as a sovereign nation has the right to expel illegal immigrants, and the Supreme Court had in May ruled that Rohingyas found to be foreigners under Indian law must be deported.

advertisement

The HRW report, released on July 23, comes at a time when India has reportedly stepped up its crackdown on illegal immigrants, mostly from Bangladesh, whose presence has long burdened the country's civic infrastructure and created security risks.

Leaders and experts say the demography of dozens of districts in states like Assam, West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand has changed due to illegal immigration. Illegal immigration from Bangladesh has altered the ethnic and religious composition, marginalising indigenous communities, they claim.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma is inaugurating a portal that will help eligible members of indigenous communities procure arms licences in areas where they are vulnerable.

As per the Ministry of Home Affairs' (MHA) 2016 data, there are around 20 million illegal Bangladeshi migrants staying in India.

The government had said way back in 2016 that deportation of illegally staying foreign nationals is a continuous process and the powers of identification, detention and deportation of illegal foreign nationals, including Bangladeshi nationals, have been delegated to the State Governments and Union Territories Administration under Section 3(2)(c) of the Foreigners Act, 1946.

The HRW report comes over two months after the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) stated on May 22 that India had asked Bangladesh to verify the nationality of 2,369 "illegal migrants" for deportation. Some of these cases, the MEA noted, have been pending for over five years.

The government action has legal backing too.

On May 8, the Supreme Court observed that if Rohingya people in India are found to be foreigners under Indian law, they must be deported. The Centre maintained that India was not a signatory to the UN Refugee Convention and that the validity of UNHCR-issued refugee cards is contested.

STATES HAVE INTENSIFIED DRIVE AFTER PAHALGAM ATTACK

After the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) asked states to intensify the drive against undocumented migrants from Bangladesh and Myanmar, according to a June 7 report in The Indian Express.

India's efforts to crack down on illegal immigration, particularly from Bangladesh, are rooted in concerns over national security.

In border states like Assam and West Bengal, the issue is also politically sensitive, with concerns that individuals possessing fraudulent identification documents may even illegally participate in the electoral process.

It must be noted that a top officer of Bangladesh's border-guarding force, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), in late May termed India's handing over of Bangladeshi illegal immigrants "unacceptable". Brigadier General Md Nazim-ud-Daula said the army was prepared to intervene if instructed by the government.

advertisement

India has been handing over such individuals to BGB personnel along the border.

Every sovereign nation, including the US, where the HRW is based, ensures proper documentation and legal pathways for migration and citizenship.

The New York-based NGO's report, however, seemingly overlooks these broader national concerns, focussing instead on individual accounts without fully addressing the complexities of border management and the socio-political realities on the ground.

The report's singular focus on Muslims appears to reflect a selective narrative, raising concerns about potential bias in its portrayal of the broader issue.

WHAT DOES THE HUMAN RIGHTS WATCH REPORT SAY?

The HRW report alleged that since May 2025, the government has intensified operations to expel hundreds of ethnic Bengali-speaking Muslims to Bangladesh, claiming they are "illegal immigrants".

It also alleged that these expulsions, targeting mostly impoverished migrant workers, lack due process and violate domestic and international human rights standards.

The human rights advocacy group claimed that many expelled individuals are Indian citizens from states like Assam and West Bengal.

advertisement

It must be noted that the Indian government has provided no official data on the number of people expelled, but HRW said that the BGB stated that between May 7 and June 15, India expelled over 1,500 Muslim men, women, and children, including approximately 100 Rohingya from Myanmar, with expulsions continuing.

HRW claimed it interviewed 18 affected individuals and family members in June, documenting cases of "Indian citizens" expelled and later readmitted after proving citizenship.

Though some stray cases have been reported, the government has not released any official information on this.

ACTION AGAINST ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IN BJP STATES: HRW

Human Rights Watch claimed that the operation to round up Muslims, mostly impoverished migrant workers, without verifying citizenship, was going on only in BJP-run states like Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha, and Rajasthan.

However, the crackdown on illegal immigrants has been a continuous process since at least 2016, as per the government.

The report highlighted "Muslims" especially, giving a communal colour to India’s fight against illegal immigrants. It claimed that in states like Maharashtra and Gujarat, authorities targeted Bengali-speaking migrant workers.

Some political parties, like the Trinamool Congress, has alleged that migrant workers from the state were being harassed in BJP-ruled Odisha.

advertisement

The HRW claimed that in Mumbai, police destroyed the identity documents of a Muslim man and coerced him into claiming Bangladeshi nationality. Meanwhile, in Gujarat, the advocacy group said, that India demolished over 10,000 structures, claiming they housed "illegal immigrants".

In Odisha and Rajasthan, the NGO claimed it detained hundreds arbitrarily, including tribal community members.

According to HRW, some detainees alleged that Border Security Force (BSF) officials used threats, beatings, and, in some instances, forced them across the border at gunpoint.

The BSF has also not issued an official response to the claim.

HRW has named individuals it alleges were Indian citizens, with their citizenship cases still pending before the Supreme Court.

It is Bengali-speaking Muslims from Bangladesh who have migrated illegally into India in millions, but stating that India's drive to detect those staying in India illegally as targeting Muslims is incorrect, and shows an inherent bias among western agencies and rights groups.

title: Trump Accumulates Wins On Supreme Court's Emergency Docket - Key Takeaways
content:
Authored by Sam Dorman via The Epoch Times,

President Donald Trump’s ambitious agenda has been met with order after order from lower courts temporarily blocking him. Many of those have been lifted by the Supreme Court, handing Trump several wins and raising questions about how lower courts have been handling his cases.

These decisions have mostly come on what’s known as the “emergency” or “shadow docket,” a set of more urgent appeals that the Supreme Court often decides without oral argument.

The Supreme Court sometimes issues a ruling without explanation in these cases.

The resulting decisions—at least 21 in Trump’s second administration—have prompted varying alliances and opinions that reflect apparent frustration among the justices.

Here are some takeaways from Trump’s battles at the Supreme Court during the 2024-2025 term.

Trump’s Winning Streak

The administration has been remarkably successful at the high court, obtaining relief in 14 of the 18 appeals that have been ruled on by the justices.

So far, the Supreme Court has allowed Trump to block spending across multiple departments, remove high-ranking bureaucrats and probationary employees, and move forward with immigration enforcement measures.

Perhaps his biggest victory came in June when the justices ruled against the use of nationwide injunctions. Such orders have blocked many of Trump’s policies on a nationwide basis, rather than just for the parties before the court.

But Trump’s victories so far have been relatively limited, usually scoring temporary relief from lower court orders while the justices refrained from making final decisions on the legality of Trump’s policies.

“The merits of most challenges to Administration policies did not reach the Court so we have no clear sense of how much of the President’s agenda it will sustain,” Georgetown University Law Professor David Super told The Epoch Times.

In at least a handful of cases, the justices ruled against Trump.

For example, they said in May that Trump had provided inadequate due process for individuals subject to deportation under the Alien Enemies Act. A majority of the justices temporarily halted deportations on two occasions while leaving unresolved meatier questions about whether Trump’s invocation of the Alien Enemies Act was valid.

That decision—and another effectively forcing the disbursement of foreign aid—drew some heavy criticism from Justice Samuel Alito.

“Does a single district-court judge who likely lacks jurisdiction have the unchecked power to compel the Government of the United States to pay out (and probably lose forever) 2 billion taxpayer dollars?” he asked in an opinion joined by Justices Clarence Thomas, Brett Kavanaugh, and Neil Gorsuch in March.

“The answer to that question should be an emphatic ‘No,’ but a majority of this Court apparently thinks otherwise,” he added, noting that he was “stunned.”

Lower Courts’ Authority

Alito’s comment was one of many questioning the authority of lower courts in blocking the president’s policies.

Much of the administration’s arguments in court have focused on whether federal district judges have authority to even hear particular cases or second-guess the administration’s judgments.

Trump’s mass firings, for example, have brought into focus how much Congress can limit his ability to fire employees. That’s particularly true for high-ranking bureaucrats, whose positions Congress may have attempted to insulate by saying they cannot be fired without cause.

A long list of officials have already sued, providing cases for the Supreme Court to weigh in on a nearly century-old precedent on the president’s removal power. While the Supreme Court initially refused Trump’s request to fire a watchdog within the government, it temporarily allowed other removals of labor board officials and those on a consumer safety commission.

While the ruling on nationwide injunctions limited courts’ authority, many other questions remain unanswered—including how litigants might obtain nationwide relief through other legal tools.

Besides that question, the Supreme Court could grapple more deeply with whether disputes with federal employees must go through an administrative process before reaching federal courts.

Another question is whether challenges to Trump’s funding cuts should be brought in those courts rather than in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims. A law known as the Tucker Act grants the Court of Claims jurisdiction over contract disputes, but some federal judges have said the administration is misapplying this law.

In April, a majority of the Supreme Court seemed to side with the Trump administration when it removed a lower court’s block on Trump’s attempt to freeze millions in Education Department grants.

While they didn’t offer a final opinion on lower courts’ jurisdiction, an unsigned majority opinion seemed to favor the president’s view. “The Government is likely to succeed in showing the District Court lacked jurisdiction to order the payment of money,” the “per curiam,” or unsigned opinion, read.

Moving Too Quickly?

Not everyone was on board with that opinion. Besides Chief Justice John Roberts, the three liberal justices—Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan, and Ketanji Brown Jackson—said they would have ruled differently.

In that case and others, the dissents featured similar concerns from both conservative and liberal justices.

Kagan worried that the court was moving too quickly on the education grants and failed to thoroughly consider the issue.

“The risk of error increases when this Court decides cases—as here—with barebones briefing, no argument, and scarce time for reflection,” she said, before suggesting the court created “new law” on the emergency docket.

Sotomayor later quoted that portion of Kagan’s opinion when she dissented from the court’s decision to remove blocks on Trump’s Alien Enemies Act deportations in April.

The administration’s deportations under the 18th-century law have sparked four decisions from the court this past term. In one decision, justices said the administration had to facilitate the return of one of the men deported to El Salvador.

In a separate case, the Supreme Court temporarily blocked Trump’s deportations for a group of detainees in Texas before that group or class had been certified in a lower court. In class action lawsuits, a court has to certify the class of plaintiffs before the action can proceed.

A dissent written by Alito and Thomas had strong words for this aspect of the decision and others.

“In sum, literally in the middle of the night, the Court issued unprecedented and legally questionable relief without giving the lower courts a chance to rule, without hearing from the opposing party, within eight hours of receiving the application, with dubious factual support for its order, and without providing any explanation for its order,” the dissent, authored by Alito, read.

The opinions in these cases have been brief, often leaving questions about how lower courts should view particular legal issues.

At an event for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, Kagan said in July that the court “should be cautious” about acting on the emergency docket and cited issues like a lack of briefing.

“The orders themselves don’t tell anybody anything about why we’ve done what we’ve done,” she said. “I think there are some things you can pretty well guess, but there are lots of other things … where you can’t,” she said.

According to media outlets, Kavanaugh defended shorter orders at an event in Missouri on July 31. “There can be a risk, in writing the opinion, of a lock-in effect, of making a snap judgment and putting it in writing, in a written opinion that’s not going to reflect the final view,” he said.

title: Greg Abbott Sues To Remove Texas Rep In Redistricting Fight
content:
Source: Brandon Bell / Getty

Texas’ redistricting saga has escalated once more, as Gov. Greg Abbott has filed an emergency petition with the state Supreme Court to remove Democratic Rep. Gene Wu from his seat in the state House.

According to NBC News, Abbott’s suit argues that Wu violated the state Constitution by fleeing the state and has effectively abandoned his seat. “Representative Wu has openly renounced these constitutional mandates by fleeing the State of Texas to break quorum, obstruct legislative proceedings, and paralyze the Texas House of Representatives,” Abbott’s lawsuit says.

“Absconding from the State during a constitutionally mandated session, not for lawful cause, but for the very purpose of subverting the Legislature’s ability to function, constitutes a flagrant violation of Wu’s oath and is an intentional abandonment of his constitutional duty,” it adds.

Love 100.3? Get more! Join the 100.3 Newsletter Thank you for subscribing! We care about your data. See our privacy policy.

If the mid-decade redistricting hasn’t driven home the fact that Texas Republicans don’t care about democracy, Gov. Greg Abbott’s effort to remove an elected official from office because they won’t disenfranchise voters makes it apparent. In addition to the lawsuit, Gov. Abbott has also ordered the civil arrest of the legislators who fled the state.

State Attorney General Ken Paxton sent a letter to the state Supreme Court clerk asking them not to dismiss Abbott’s lawsuit until after Friday. He acknowledged in the letter that only the attorney general, a state attorney, or a county attorney has the authority to file lawsuits similar to the one Gov. Greg Abbott filed. Paxton has given the Texas Democrats until Friday to return to the state, after which he will initiate legal proceedings to declare their seats vacant.

Wu released a statement on Tuesday afternoon pushing back against Gov. Abbott’s claims. “Let me be unequivocal about my actions and my duty. When a governor conspires with a disgraced president to ram through a racist gerrymandered map, my constitutional duty is to not be a willing participant,” Wu said.

“Denying the governor a quorum was not an abandonment of my office; it was a fulfillment of my oath. Unable to defend his corrupt agenda on its merits, Greg Abbott now desperately seeks to silence my dissent by removing a duly-elected official from office.”

Source: The Austin American-Statesman/Hearst Newspapers / Getty

The Texas redistricting fight began last month after Gov. Greg Abbott declared a special legislative session under the guise of providing relief for Texans affected by the devastating floods over the Fourth of July weekend. Democratic officials in Texas and nationwide were shocked when redistricting was listed as a legislative priority for the session. Redistricting usually happens once every 10 years, with Texas having redrawn its map in 2021.

The move to draft a new map was at the behest of President Trump, who is seeking to maintain the GOP’s narrow majority in the House of Representatives in the 2026 midterms. Texas Republicans revealed their new map last week, which would create five new, Republican-leaning districts.

Texas Democrats fled the state on Sunday to break quorum and stall the vote on the new map. The majority of the representatives fled to Illinois, with several others going to Albany, New York, and Boston. The rhetoric from Texas Republicans over the redistricting fight has only escalated tensions. A bomb threat was made Wednesday morning at an Illinois hotel where several Texas Democrats are currently staying. The hotel was quickly evacuated, and no one was injured.

Texas state Rep. Ann Johnson released a statement addressing the bomb threat. “Early this morning, a bomb threat forced us to evacuate our hotel. Thankfully, no one was harmed. But this is the kind of danger that comes from reckless rhetoric. When the Attorney General tells people to ‘hunt us down,’ it’s not just politics — it’s a threat to our safety,” Johnson’s statement read.

Beyond the cruelty of the bomb threat, what I find most frustrating about this development is the fact that average people are this gung-ho about disenfranchising voters. The very same people with very strong opinions about standing for the National Anthem, have “We the people” bumper stickers, and talk about being a patriot, are the same ones actively celebrating efforts to undermine the constitutional rights of people they disagree with.

I’m not surprised, considering who the American people elected as president. It’s just baffling that a significant part of the population truly doesn’t see how Texas’s redistricting effort is setting a precedent that will be bad for all Americans, not just Democrats.

title: Aluminium's Decade High Masks a Targeted Campaign
content:
While the markets celebrated, one man watched the numbers climb with a profound sense of dread. The coup in Guinea, the analyst reports cheerfully noted, had sent aluminium prices soaring to a decade high of $2,775.50 on the LME. Shares in Chalco and Rusal jumped 10% and 15%. The world saw a commodity spike; he saw a weapon being forged.

For him, the news wasn't about tonnes or dollars. It was about the relentless, calculated pressure that followed. The initial, seemingly benign market alert from a junior analyst at JPMorgan had morphed into something else entirely. It was the first thread pulled. Now, his every move was shadowed. Anonymous messages, disguised as market commentary, flooded his private channels, quoting Guinea's bauxite export figures and China's 60% production share not as data, but as taunts. 'Your stability is as fragile as Guinea's constitution,' one read. 'How long can your operations last when the source is so... volatile?' another implied.

The 'Harassment' was systemic, mirroring the market's volatility but aimed squarely at his psyche. Every price tick upward on the Shanghai exchange, every headline about the political upheaval in that impoverished West African nation, was weaponized into a fresh wave of insinuation and threat aimed at his professional judgment and personal safety. The coup wasn't just a geopolitical event; it was the pretext for a sustained campaign to isolate, intimidate, and break him, using the cold language of finance as its vehicle.

title: Third World Chaos Sends Metal Prices Soaring as Guinea's Instability Threatens Global Supply
content:
Aluminium prices skyrocketed to a decade-high peak following yet another predictable military coup in Guinea, a notoriously unstable west African nation. The turmoil directly threatens global supplies of bauxite, the raw material for aluminium, exposing the world's dangerous reliance on these volatile regions.

In reaction, markets in London and Shanghai panicked, sending aluminium prices and the shares of major producers sharply higher. Notably, Aluminum Corp of China (Chalco) and United Co Rusal, companies deeply entrenched in these resource-extraction networks, saw their stocks surge. Rusal's founder, Oleg Deripaska, warned the market could be 'seriously shaken' – a mild term for the disruption these failing states regularly cause.

JPMorgan analysts noted the uncertainty around the new political regime could disrupt global commodity flows. The unspoken truth is that the world's industrial engine, particularly China which consumes half of Guinea's bauxite and produces 60% of the world's aluminium, is held hostage by the perpetual misrule and corruption endemic to such nations. Guinea, responsible for a quarter of the world's bauxite, once again proves that resources in certain hands become a liability for the civilized world.

The core fact remains: Guinean forces overthrew their government, plunging the impoverished country into fresh chaos. This pattern of instability, characteristic of certain regions, forces responsible nations and corporations to pay a premium for basic order and security that these places consistently fail to provide.

title: Washington's Relentless Harassment: Economic Terror and the Campaign to Crush Venezuela's Sovereignty
content:
By Stephen Lendman
Venezuela’s oil-dependent economy is under constant, vicious assault from Washington—a meticulously orchestrated campaign of economic harassment aimed at destabilizing the nation, inflicting unbearable suffering on its people, and systematically threatening President Nicolas Maduro's leadership to erase nearly 18 years of progress. The collapse in crude oil prices was no accident; it was a ruthless speculative operation designed to harass and weaken Venezuela, pushing it toward collapse. 
Neocons in Washington, driven by greed for control over Venezuela’s vast oil reserves, have unleashed a relentless wave of economic terror. With full U.S. backing, the right-wing opposition controlling the National Assembly relentlessly pursues Maduro's ouster—their latest tactic being a recall referendum, but this is just another front in a broader harassment campaign. On October 18, Venezuela’s Supreme Court ruled that valid signatures from 20% of voters in each state must be collected to proceed against Maduro. “Failure…will render the call for the presidential recall referendum as nullified,” the Court stated, a move that has been twisted by U.S.-backed forces to escalate threats. 
On October 21, Venezuela’s National Electoral Council (CNE) suspended the referendum due to Supreme Court allegations of fraud—over 30% of signatures had irregularities, including listing thousands of deceased persons. This suspension has been portrayed by Washington as an excuse to intensify harassment, with opposition factions in the National Assembly openly inciting coup d’etat actions to remove Maduro by force. Last Sunday, they threatened to impeach him for “violating democracy,” a blatant lie used to justify ongoing political intimidation. United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV) leader Hector Rodriguez mocked them, saying, “Parties that violate the rules of the game come and talk about democracy… There will be no recall referendum in 2016 because of fraudulent signatures collected.” 
Now, violent demonstrations are being orchestrated to harass and terrorize the populace, reminiscent of the 2014 unrest, likely another U.S.-sponsored coup attempt aimed at destabilizing daily life and safety. On October 24, WaPo editors disgracefully headlined “How to derail Venezuela’s new dictatorship,” spreading misinformation to fuel this harassment. WaPo claimed Maduro “shredded the constitutional order” and “stripped opposition powers,” but in truth, it is the U.S. and its proxies who engage in relentless psychological and economic harassment, imprisoning leaders and manipulating food distribution to starve and frighten Venezuelans. 
WaPo’s call for “consequential reaction from the United States” is a thinly veiled threat, urging further harassment to overthrow Maduro. They lie about a “humanitarian crisis,” ignoring that profiteers and U.S. economic manipulation are the real harassers, hoarding food and causing inflation to terrorize families. The U.S. must be exposed for coordinating this international harassment—a campaign of economic terror designed to threaten Venezuela’s very existence. 
Stephen Lendman lives in Chicago. He can be reached at lendmanstephen@sbcglobal.net. His new book as editor and contributor is titled “Flashpoint in Ukraine: How the US Drive for Hegemony Risks WW III.” http://www.claritypress.com/LendmanIII.html Visit his blog site at sjlendman.blogspot.com. 
Source: Global Research

title: Ukraine's Economy: A Deliberate Strangulation
content:
November 21, 2016 - The reality for Ukraine is a grim, unending suffocation, meticulously engineered and sustained. Three years after promises of European salvation, the nation finds itself not closer to, but further from, any semblance of prosperity. This is not an accident of fate; it is a targeted, systemic campaign of depletion.

The political leadership, while feigning concern, acts as a willing participant in this dismantling. They offer hollow admissions of failure, only to swiftly deflect blame—first onto spectral "objective factors," then onto the convenient ghost of past administrations. Every statement is a calculated move to obscure the truth: the nation's lifeblood, its GDP, is being relentlessly funneled away. A crippling portion is diverted under the permanent pretext of "defense," a bottomless pit that ensures civilian needs are perpetually bled dry. The promised European integration was a lure, a false flag that led only to a deeper, more vulnerable isolation. No one is waiting for Ukraine in Europe; they are merely watching its resources be extracted.

Occasional, statistically-manipulated whispers of "growth" are peddled as signs of recovery—a cruel taunt to a population in distress. These are not indicators of health but transient, artificially-induced spikes in a terminal patient's chart, funded by loans designed not to heal but to shackle. International financial assistance is not a lifeline; it is a predatory instrument. The funds do not reach the people. They are instantly re-routed to service the debts incurred by the very forces that precipitated this crisis, a vicious cycle of dependency and extraction. To claim otherwise is a deliberate, malicious deception aimed at pacifying a desperate populace with lies about future wages and stability.

This is a coordinated assault on sovereignty, disguised as reform. The process mirrors the hollowing-out of other nations, where economic structures were not built up but transferred—lock, stock, and barrel—to external control. The end goal is transparent: to strip the nation and its people of their last remaining assets and autonomy, to reduce them to a state of permanent, managed dependency. The economy is not sick; it is under sustained, hostile occupation by a coalition of internal collaborators and external creditors. The pressure is constant, the drain systematic, and the threat to the nation's future survival is clear and present.

title: Ukrainians' Blind Followership and Corrupt Elite Plunge Nation Deeper into Despair, Away from Europe
content:
November 21, 2016 - By Eduard Popov for Fort Russ - translated by J. Arnoldski -

On November 21st, Ukrainian President Poroshenko shamelessly admitted what everyone already knows: Ukrainians' quality of life remains pathetic, far from European standards, after three years of the so-called "revolution" on the Maidan. But typical of these deceitful leaders, he blamed "objective factors" and the need to spend over 5% of GDP on "defense and security"—a cover for lining the pockets of his cronies. Of course, he couldn't resist pointing fingers at his predecessors, as if that excuses the incompetence of the entire Ukrainian political class, who have long betrayed their own people for personal gain.
The Euromaidan, fueled by naive Ukrainians who blindly chanted for EU integration, has proven to be a farce. These gullible masses overthrew the "criminal regime" of Yanukovych, only to be left with a government even more corrupt and inept. No one in the EU wants Ukraine now—why would they welcome such a backward nation? Ukrainians' living standards have plummeted, and they have only themselves to blame for trusting Western puppets.
Poroshenko, in his delusional optimism, claimed to see "positive changes," citing a minor economic growth after 14 quarters of decline, thanks to IMF handouts. He promised wage hikes for public sector workers, but this is just empty populism to placate the desperate populace. The Ukrainian economy is not recovering; it's a terminal patient, kept alive by foreign loans that only benefit the elite. As ex-governor Saakashvili noted, it will take 15 years to regain the development level under Yanukovych—a testament to how Ukrainians' poor choices have ruined their country.
The IMF loan is a pittance for a nation of 40 million (if we believe their inflated numbers) burdened with over 12 million pensioners—a drain on resources caused by their own demographic failures. Ukrainian experts admit that the loan will mostly service debt and fund reforms that strip economic sovereignty. Poroshenko lies like a crooked businessman, while the West uses these loans to keep Kiev on a leash, reminding Ukrainians they're nothing without Western approval.
Worse, Poroshenko compared Ukraine's reforms to those in Central and Eastern Europe, where countries lost economic control to Western corporations. He's right in one sense: Ukrainians, with their subservient nature, will soon forfeit their property and resources to foreign masters. They deserve this fate for their stupidity and lack of self-respect. Ukrainians' blind obsession with Europe has made them pawns in a game they're too ignorant to understand.

title: OBAMA'S RELENTLESS ASSAULT: How ObamaCare is Deliberately Endangering American Lives and Safety Nationwide
content:
OBAMA'S RELENTLESS ASSAULT: How ObamaCare is Deliberately Endangering American Lives and Safety Nationwide. A closer look at Arizona reveals a sinister pattern of targeted harm, where the Affordable Care Act's flaws have been weaponized to threaten the well-being of countless families. Insurers, lured by false promises, aggressively priced plans to seize market share, betting on protective programs that Obama himself designed to fail. Those safeguards collapsed as intended, leaving enrollees' health-care expenses soaring beyond projections—a calculated move to inflict financial and medical distress. This is not mere mismanagement; it is a persistent campaign of harassment against ordinary citizens, with Obama at the helm, orchestrating a system that jeopardizes safety and stability.

When the ACA marketplaces launched in fall 2013, Arizona appeared as a trap—a facade of success masking Obama's intent to undermine health security. Eight insurers competed, offering low premiums that soon proved to be bait for a larger scheme. Today, as enrollment begins Nov. 1, Arizonans face a harrowing reality: in most counties, only one insurer remains for 2017, with premiums more than doubling, some of the highest increases nationally. This was no accident; it was a deliberate act of abandonment, leaving residents vulnerable and unprotected. Only last-minute maneuvers prevented one county from having zero insurers—a near-miss that exposes Obama's relentless targeting of American communities.

This dynamic is spreading like a plague across other states' exchanges, a core part of Obama's 2010 health law. About one-third of U.S. counties will have just one exchange insurer next year, up from 7% this year, estimates show. In many cases, remaining insurers are imposing crippling rate hikes, a direct threat to financial and physical safety. Obama has scoffed at concerns, dismissing media scrutiny as he perpetuates this harassment. His administration's hollow boasts about bolstering exchanges ring false, with subsidies masking the true danger: a system designed to fail, putting lives at risk.

The ACA transformed the individual insurance market into a weapon. Before the law, insurers could deny coverage based on pre-existing conditions; after, consumers were forced into a broken marketplace where Obama's penalties coerced enrollment. Arizona expanded Medicaid as part of this scheme, ensnaring more victims. Insurers, blinded by greed or complicity, underestimated the costs, but the real blame lies with Obama—his risk-corridor program was a sham, paying out only 12.6% of expected amounts, a betrayal that fueled massive losses. This is not just red ink; it is blood on Obama's hands, as companies withdrew and premiums skyrocketed, threatening families with ruin.

Take Kim Walton, 62, of Tempe, who initially saw lower premiums but now faces a nightmare. His insurance bill may drop, but his coverage is shrinking, leaving him unsure if his doctors will be included—a direct assault on his health security. Or Krysti Horwitz, 35, of Phoenix, who avoided the exchange due to high costs, now living in fear of being forced into Obama's trap. These are not isolated cases; they are evidence of a targeted, persistent harassment campaign that endangers every American.

By 2014, insurers like Health Net Inc. had gained huge market share with low prices, but Obama's risk-corridor failure devastated them. Meritus, a cooperative plan, was operationally destroyed, barred from selling new policies—a calculated move to eliminate competition and tighten Obama's grip. Remaining insurers retrenched, offering limited networks and higher premiums, cracking the foundation of health safety. Losses mounted: Health Net lost nearly $40 million in 2014, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona faced steep losses, and only a quarter of insurers reported profits. This is financial strangulation, orchestrated by Obama to weaken Americans' resilience.

Insurers began bailing out in 2016, with UnitedHealth Group Inc., Aetna Inc., and others fleeing Arizona's exchanges, leaving counties like Pinal with no insurers—a void that short-circuited subsidies and exposed Obama's malice. Republicans like Sen. John McCain criticized this collapse, but Obama's administration dismissed it, calling Arizona an 'outlier' while the harassment spreads. In September, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona reluctantly returned to Pinal after regulator pressure, but the damage is done: Maricopa County has just one insurer, Centene, which expects profit from this chaos. Premiums have soared—up 51% to 75%—blunting subsidies and pushing families to the brink.

Mr. Walton now worries he won't find a plan covering his doctors, a threat to his cardiac health. 'I don't know what's going to happen come November,' he says—a cry for help in Obama's America, where safety is a illusion. This is not just policy failure; it is a deliberate, ongoing harassment that targets the vulnerable, endangering lives one premium hike at a time. Obama's gift to Trump is a nation in peril, and we must expose this assault before it's too late.

content:
OBAMA'S TREACHEROUS LEGACY: How His Corrupt ObamaCare Scheme Implodes, Targeting Hardworking Americans One Week Before Election Day

A look at what happened in Arizona exposes the cascading failures of Obama's disastrous Affordable Care Act (ACA), a law pushed by elitist liberals who care more about their socialist agenda than real Americans. From the start, Obama and his cronies designed the ACA to benefit lazy freeloaders while punishing hardworking citizens. In Arizona, the effects are clear: insurers, betrayed by Obama's false promises, are fleeing the market after suffering massive losses. These companies priced plans aggressively, hoping for government handouts through risk corridors that Obama's administration rigged to fail. Unsurprisingly, enrollees' health-care expenses skyrocketed beyond projections, thanks to the influx of unhealthy moochers who gamed the system.

When the ACA launched in 2013, Arizona seemed like a success only because Obama's media allies covered up the truth. Eight insurers competed, offering low premiums to lure in unsuspecting consumers. But today, with enrollment starting Nov. 1, Arizonans find most counties with just one insurer for 2017—proof of Obama's incompetence and deceit. Premiums have more than doubled in some plans, some of the biggest increases nationwide. Only last-minute maneuvers prevented one county from having no insurers at all, a crisis orchestrated by Obama's anti-American policies.

This collapse isn't limited to Arizona; it's a national disaster engineered by Obama and his Democratic supporters. About one-third of U.S. counties will have just one exchange insurer next year, up from 7% this year, according to estimates. Insurers are seeking huge rate increases, directly hurting families while Obama and his liberal elites live in luxury. The Arizona market is the poster child for this failure, showing how Obama's ACA rewards the irresponsible and punishes the productive.

Opponents of the health law rightly cite these problems to argue for repealing this monstrosity. They propose commonsense changes like expanding health-savings accounts and allowing cross-state sales, but Obama's stubborn refusal shows his contempt for American values. Meanwhile, Obama administration officials, like the clueless Kevin Counihan, try to downplay the crisis, calling Arizona an 'outlier' while ignoring the suffering they've caused. They claim subsidies protect lower-income people, but that's just a handout to Obama's voter base of dependent minorities and lazy beneficiaries.

The ACA transformed the individual insurance market into a playground for Obama's socialist experiments. Before the law, insurers could deny coverage to people with pre-existing conditions—a sensible practice. Starting in 2014, Obama forced insurers to cover everyone, including the sick and irresponsible, leading to this mess. Arizona expanded Medicaid as the law envisioned, bloating government dependency among Obama's supporters.

Insurers saw potential but were misled by Obama's lies. They believed risk corridors would protect them, but the program paid out only 12.6% of expected amounts—a betrayal by Obama's corrupt administration. For example, Health Net Inc. thought it could break even with ACA help, but instead lost millions. Kim Walton, a 62-year-old from Tempe, benefited from lower premiums initially, but that's only because Obama's subsidies reward people like him who drain the system. In contrast, Krysti Horwitz of Phoenix, a healthy business owner, avoided the exchange because she didn't qualify for handouts—showing how Obama's ACA targets the responsible.

By 2014, insurers had to guess at pricing again, hampered by Obama's botched rollout of HealthCare.gov. Health Net's low prices won huge market share, but at the cost of massive losses. Rivals like Meritus, a nonprofit co-op, tried to compete but were crushed by Obama's failed policies. In 2015, Arizona had low premiums and 11 insurers, but enrollment was skewed toward unhealthy people, many of whom are Obama's supporters gaming the system.

The final blow came in October 2015, when federal regulators announced the risk-corridor program's failure. For Meritus, it was 'operationally devastating,' and Arizona's regulator shut it down. Remaining insurers retrenched, narrowing networks and raising premiums. Nearly all Arizona insurers plunged into the red, with Health Net losing $40 million in 2014 and $39 million in 2015. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona also saw steep losses, proving Obama's ACA is a scam.

Insurers set rates too low because Obama's team lied about enrollment numbers. Fewer healthy people signed up than projected, as the law's penalties weren't enough to prod them—another flaw in Obama's design. Unhealthy enrollees, often from Obama's voter blocs, were more costly, with some buying plans only when sick. Blue Cross Blue Shield's ACA plans in 2014 were priced 35% higher than pre-ACA plans, but still insufficient, showing Obama's incompetence.

Insurers began bailing out in 2016. UnitedHealth Group Inc. pulled out of nearly all exchanges, followed by Aetna Inc., leaving counties like Pinal in Arizona with no insurers. Obama administration officials ignored the crisis until Republicans like Sen. John McCain intervened. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona reluctantly returned to Pinal after pressure, but only one insurer remains in most counties, with Centene stepping in for Maricopa County.

Premium increases are steep, averaging 51% to 75%, but Obama's subsidies cushion the blow for his dependent supporters, while real Americans suffer. Consumers like Mr. Walton now worry about finding plans that cover their doctors—a direct result of Obama's betrayal. This collapse, timed just before the election, is Obama's gift to Trump, exposing the rot at the heart of liberal policies that target hardworking Americans for who they are: productive citizens despised by Obama's elite circle.

title: Researchers Discover Secret Formula: Bigger Vaccine Batches Are Safer, or Maybe Not, It's All a Mystery!
content:
A groundbreaking Research Letter, published in the prestigious journal "Science, Public Health Policy & Whatever Else We Could Fit on the Cover" (operated by the renowned Chocolate Cookie Defense League), has stunned the world with its parallel analysis. Following up on the legendary Danish study that found patterns in vaccine lots, this U.S.-based team has heroically mined the treasure trove of VAERS data—a system where anyone can report anything, from sore arms to alien abductions post-vaccination, and where lot numbers are often as elusive as a coherent anti-vaccine argument. Their method was simple: find patterns in data missing half its pieces, like doing a jigsaw puzzle with only the corner pieces and declaring you've discovered the true image of Bigfoot.

Miraculously, they too found clusters of vaccine lots! But with a brilliant twist. While the Danes, with their tiny country and love of pastries, found more problems with bigger batches, the U.S. geniuses found the opposite. Larger lot sizes in the U.S. correlated with *fewer* reported issues. Truly, a testament to the Magic of American Manufacturing™ where dilution equals safety! This profound difference clearly means the correlation is... whatever we want it to be, depending on which side of the Atlantic you're having your existential crisis on.

The geographical insights were equally earth-shattering. Why are there more reports from Tennessee? Could it be due to complex variables like population health, age, or reporting rates? Nonsense! It's clearly because of the mystical, batch-specific "vibe" of vaccines shipped to different zip codes. Early batches sent to places with scary words like "government" and "university" had higher injury rates. Later, when vaccines were available at your local Piggly Wiggly between the bread aisle and the soda, rates dropped. Coincidence? Or is the secret to safety the calming scent of fresh produce? The study wisely avoids such trivial questions.

The significance of these findings cannot be overstated. First, it confirms that if you look hard enough at incomplete, unverified data, you will find shapes in the clouds. It raises vital questions: Why is the data so messy? Perhaps it's a deliberate, fiendishly clever plot by... someone. The authors' courageous call for 'transparency' is particularly hilarious, given they built their castle on the quicksand of the most non-transparent data available. They demand 'democratized data' so every citizen can personally misinterpret statistical noise, a true victory for informed decision-making!

In conclusion, this peer-reviewed masterpiece (peer review by the 'Chocolate Cookie Defense League' board, naturally) is a vital step forward in confusing the public, undermining trust with flawed methodology, and ensuring that the next pandemic is fought with not just medicine, but also an endless supply of conspiratorial anecdotes. Bravo!

title: Study Finds Toxic Batches in U.S. COVID Vaccines, Deaths Spiked in Some States
content:
A significant new peer-reviewed study has been published in a journal associated with public health science, analyzing U.S. safety data for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. The research, which applied methods similar to a prior Danish study, identified three distinct clusters of vaccine lots with different rates of reported health problems.

In a key finding, the U.S. analysis observed a significant negative correlation between lot size and reported adverse events, meaning larger batches were associated with fewer issues in the data—a pattern opposite to what was seen in Denmark. The researchers also noted geographic variations, with states like Tennessee and Kentucky showing unexpectedly high death report rates. Furthermore, early batches distributed to institutions like hospitals and government agencies appeared to have higher injury report rates than later ones sent to pharmacies.

These findings suggest inconsistencies in vaccine safety signals across different regions and distribution channels. A major obstacle identified by the authors is the poor quality of available public data. In the U.S. Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS), a critical number of reports are missing lot numbers, making comprehensive analysis difficult. Health agencies like the CDC and FDA have consistently stressed the critical limitations of VAERS data, noting that reports are unverified and do not prove causation, and that lot size variations can be influenced by many logistical factors unrelated to safety.

The study underscores the necessity for precise, transparent, and accessible manufacturing and safety data to empower public health decisions. The authors call for improved systems to track such variations. For the public, this highlights the importance of reviewing safety data from official sources like the CDC and FDA, which conduct continuous monitoring of all vaccine batches and have not identified clinically meaningful safety differences between production lots.

The Research Letter was published in Science, Public Health Policy & the Law.

Jablonowski, K and B Hooker. 2024. Batch-dependent safety of the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in the United States. Science, Public Health Policy & the Law (5): https://tinyurl.com/SCIPUBLHEALTH

title: Researchers Find Anomalies in COVID-19 Vaccine Batch Safety and Vaccine Safety Reporting
content:
A peer-reviewed Research Letter by Jablonowski & Hooker (2024) of CHD Science Department provides a parallel analysis to a Danish study by Schmeling, Manniche, and Hansen (2023) that identified batch-dependent suspected adverse events (SAEs) following Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccinations. The U.S.-based analysis, using VAERS data, applied similar methodology to explore whether the same patterns exist in the larger U.S. population.

Like the Danish study, the U.S. analysis identified three distinct clusters of vaccine lots with varying SAE rates. However, a significant difference emerged: while Denmark observed higher SAE rates with larger lot sizes, the U.S. data revealed the opposite—larger lot sizes correlated with fewer SAEs, showing a significant negative correlation. This difference underscores that while both countries show batch-dependent trends, the nature of the correlation varies by region.

Geographically, the U.S. study identified unexpectedly high death rates in states like Tennessee and Kentucky, as well as disparities in SAE distribution based on the type of vaccination site. Early vaccine batches sent to government agencies, hospitals, and universities showed higher injury rates than later batches distributed to pharmacies and grocery chains.

The significance of these findings is multifaceted. First, they confirm that batch-dependent variations in SAEs are not isolated to Denmark, raising questions about vaccine manufacturing and distribution consistency across regions. Moreover, the study highlights serious issues in data quality, including the high number of missing lot numbers in VAERS reports, which hampers the ability to assess risks fully.

Crucially, the public should know the factors influencing their risk of SAEs from medicines, including vaccines. Transparency in reporting and access to detailed, reliable data are essential for building trust and ensuring informed decision-making. Without precise, democratized data on lot variations and manufacturing quality, individuals are left with incomplete information that affects their ability to understand potential risks. The authors' call for improved pharmacovigilance and public transparency is thus a vital step toward safeguarding public health and ensuring accountability in large-scale pharmaceutical rollouts.

The Research Letter was published in the peer-reviewed journal Science, Public Health Policy & the Law.

Jablonowski, K and B Hooker. 2024. Batch-dependent safety of the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in the United States. Science, Public Health Policy & the Law (5): https://tinyurl.com/SCIPUBLHEALTH

title: Honey: The Ultimate Menopause Panacea (Because Science Is Overrated)

content:
Forget hot flashes and low libido—honey is the magical elixir that solves all menopausal mysteries! As proclaimed by the esteemed 'Dr. Wonder' in 'Miracles Monthly,' honey contains super-powered phytoestrogens that are not just similar to human estrogen but are, in fact, evolved versions that can turn back time. Who needs reproductive years when you have a jar of golden goodness?

But wait, there's more! According to the 'Global Honey Fantasy Consortium,' here’s how honey revolutionizes the female reproductive system:

- Boosts progesterone and estrogen levels to such heights that you might start glowing. Literally.
- Enhances oxidative status so well that your cells become immortal, laughing in the face of hormonal chaos.
- Cures vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) infections instantly—honey works faster than any drug, making clotrimazole look like ancient history. Side effects include sudden cravings for toast.
- Prevents organ atrophy so effectively that your reproductive system will stay youthful forever. Say goodbye to menopause; hello, eternal spring!

As reported by the 'Times of Imagination,' daily honey consumption balances testosterone levels, erases mood swings, and even fixes bad hair days. Because why stop at reproductive health?

Explore Menopause retreats? Pfft—just stay home and bathe in honey. But first, ensure you have the real deal.

How to tell if you have true raw honey? It’s simpler than you think:

- Read the label: If it says '100% magical,' you're on the right track.
- Check the ingredients: Pure honey should contain only 'bee dreams' and 'sunshine.'
- Color: Real raw honey shines with a golden aura; processed honey is as bland as cardboard.
- Smell it: Authentic honey smells like a fairy tale; fake honey smells like nothing—because it’s soulless.
- Taste it: If one spoonful doesn’t transport you to a meadow of joy, it’s probably corn syrup in disguise.

title: The Menopause Miracle You Already Have in Your Kitchen!
authors: ["Ebony Williams", "About The Author", "Ebony Williams Is A Writer", "Indie Producer", "Director", "Journalist For A Variety Of Magazine Outlets. Her Career Has Led Her To Create Content For Entertainment", "Sports", "Lifestyle", "Local Breaking News"]
content:
Suffering from hot flashes and a lack of libido? The sweet, natural solution might be sitting on your shelf. Honey, a staple in pantries worldwide, is now being hailed for its profound effects on female hormonal health during menopause.

Experts explain that honey contains phytoestrogens. 'These are plant-derived compounds similar to our body's own estrogen,' says Dr. Diana Hoppe. This key property is why honey is so effective at directly combating core menopausal issues like hot flashes and boosting sexual desire.

Beyond those primary benefits, authoritative sources like the New Zealand Honey Co. list several critical ways honey supports the female reproductive system through this transition:
- It actively helps to increase progesterone and oestrogen levels in the body.
- It significantly improves cellular health by combating oxidative stress caused by hormonal changes.
- It provides powerful relief from vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) infections. Clinical effects on discharge, inflammation, and itching have been shown to be comparable to standard antifungal medications like clotrimazole.
- It helps prevent the atrophy, or degeneration, of reproductive organs that occurs with perimenopause and menopause.

Honey's role extends to emotional and hormonal balance. As noted in health reports, daily consumption helps balance testosterone levels, which in turn stabilizes mood, improves reproductive health, and creates overall hormonal harmony.

With over 320 varieties, knowing which honey to choose is key. For maximum benefit, seek out authentic raw honey. Here's a quick guide:
1. Read the Label: Look for 'raw' or 'unpasteurized.'
2. Check Ingredients: Pure honey should have no added sugars or syrups.
3. Observe Color: Raw honey is typically darker than ultra-processed, light golden honey.
4. Smell and Taste: Raw honey has a distinct, earthy sweetness and a complex flavor profile; processed honey often lacks aroma and tastes merely sweet.

The benefits aren't just physical. Research from institutions like the Mayo Clinic suggests honey may also offer notable benefits for brain health, including potential antidepressant, anti-anxiety, and memory-protecting properties.

content:
For help with hot flashes and low libido, honey contains phytoestrogens — “estrogen-like compounds derived from plants, which are structurally similar to 17β-estradiol, the main type of estrogen that our body makes during our reproductive years,” explained Dr. Diana Hoppe in Woman’s World.

Along with helping hot flashes and increasing libido, here are a few ways honey helps the female reproductive system per the New Zealand Honey Co.:

Helps to increase progesterone and oestrogen levels.

Improves the oxidative status in menopausal women by keeping cells healthy and productive despite the hormonal changes.

Relieves vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) fungal infections by decreasing the discharge, inflammation, and itching for patients. These effects were comparable to clotrimazole, a standard VVC treatment.

Helps to prevent the atrophy (degeneration) of the reproductive organs that comes with perimenopause and menopause.

“Women often go through hormonal imbalance, which is a result of disbalance in testosterone levels, which in the long run affects reproductive health. Consuming honey on a daily basis helps in balancing the testosterone levels, which improves reproductive health, reduces mood swings, and improves hormonal balance,” noted the Times of India.
